content.content:
node = "~26"
pnpm = "11.27.1"
rust = "1.98.1"
moon = "2.4.5"

[plugins]
moon = "source:https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moonrepo/moon/master/proto-plugin.toml"

[settings]
auto-install = true
edition = "2021"
max_width = 120
use_small_heuristics = "Max"
msrv = "1.94"
too-many-arguments-threshold = 6
too-many-lines-threshold = 150
[files]
extend-exclude = ["apps/validate/baselines/"]

[default.extend-words]
# variable abbreviations used in pattern bindings
afe = "afe"
sme = "sme"
# ratatui is a real Rust TUI library
ratatui = "ratatui"
# beng is a real Unicode CLDR numbering-system identifier (Bengali)
beng = "beng"
[advisories]
version = 2
ignore = []

[licenses]
version = 2
allow = [
    "AGPL-3.0-or-later", # this workspace's own crates
    "MIT",
    "Apache-2.0",
    "Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception",
    "ISC",
    "BSD-2-Clause",
    "BSD-3-Clause",
    "Unicode-3.0",  # unicode-ident, unicode-id-start
    "Zlib",         # foldhash (via simd-json → oxc_resolver)
    "CC0-1.0",      # notify (via watchexec)
]

[bans]
multiple-versions = "warn"
# No skips: the duplicate oxc crate family these covered came in through
# oxc_module_lexer, which pinned 0.38.x against the main family's 0.135.x.
# That dependency is gone, and cargo-deny now reports every one of those
# skips as unnecessary.
skip = []

[sources]
unknown-registry = "deny"
unknown-git = "deny"
# https://moonrepo.dev/docs/config/workspace
$schema: "https://moonrepo.dev/schemas/workspace.json"

projects:
  core: "crates/core"
  cli: "crates/cli"
  cli-npm: "packages/cli"
  crates-binding: "crates/binding"
  napi: "packages/napi"
  validate: "apps/validate"
  vite-plugin: "packages/vite-plugin"

vcs:
  client: git
  defaultBranch: main
  sync: true
  hooks:
    pre-commit:
      - '. "$HOME/.cargo/env"'
      # Defined in the justfile so the hook and `just ci` share one definition.
      # Re-run `moon sync vcs-hooks` after changing this list.
      - "just pre-commit"

telemetry: false
# https://moonrepo.dev/docs/config/toolchain
#
# moon 2.0 renamed this file from `toolchain.yml` to `toolchains.yml`. Under
# the old name moon silently ignored it, so every version declared here was
# dead config -- which is why node/pnpm/rust versions live in `.prototools`
# and are inherited below rather than restated.
$schema: "https://moonrepo.dev/schemas/toolchains.json"

node:
  versionFromPrototools: true

pnpm:
  versionFromPrototools: true

rust:
  versionFromPrototools: true
  # proto is the single source of truth for the toolchain; moon must not
  # write a competing rust-toolchain.toml into the workspace.
  syncToolchainConfig: false
# List available commands
default:
    @just --list

# Install Cargo tools required for local development
install-tools:
    cargo install cargo-nextest --locked
    cargo install cargo-llvm-cov --locked
    cargo install cargo-machete --locked
    cargo install cargo-mutants --locked
    rustup component add llvm-tools-preview

# Check the public Rust API for accidental SemVer breaks against the last
# published version. Not wired into `just ci` yet — there is no published
# baseline to diff against until v0.1.0's first real crates.io release ships.
# Install with `cargo install cargo-semver-checks --locked` once needed.
check-api:
    cargo semver-checks check-release

# Install all dependencies
install:
    pnpm install
    cargo fetch

# Build all projects. Rust crates build via one workspace-wide cargo
# invocation, not `moon run :build` — that fans out one `cargo build -p`
# per crate, and every one of those processes contends for the same
# target/ file lock, serializing what moon's own scheduler thinks is
# parallel work (confirmed via `Blocking waiting for file lock` in verbose
# output). napi/vite-plugin have no such lock to contend over, so moon
# still orchestrates those directly.
build:
    cargo build --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi
    moon run napi:build vite-plugin:build
    cargo build --release

# Run all tests (Rust + TypeScript)
test: test-rust test-ts

# Run Rust tests (via nextest, which doesn't run doctests — paired
# with `cargo test --doc` to cover those too)
test-rust:
    cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --locked
    cargo test --doc --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi

# Run TypeScript tests
test-ts:
    pnpm --filter @oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin test

# Pack the npm packages and check napi arrives only as vite-plugin's transitive dependency (pm: npm or pnpm)
verify-install pm="pnpm":
    scripts/verify-install.sh {{ pm }}

# Run benchmarks
bench:
    cargo bench --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi

# Rust and TypeScript line coverage; with a threshold, fails if either is below it
coverage threshold="": (coverage-rust threshold) (coverage-ts threshold)

# Rust coverage: writes lcov.info and prints the summary before enforcing the threshold
coverage-rust threshold="":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --locked --lcov --output-path lcov.info
    cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only
    if [[ -n "{{ threshold }}" ]]; then
      cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only --fail-under-lines "{{ threshold }}"
    fi

# TypeScript coverage: prints the summary and writes packages/vite-plugin/coverage/lcov.info
coverage-ts threshold="":
    pnpm --filter @oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin exec vitest run --coverage {{ if threshold != "" { "--coverage.thresholds.lines=" + threshold } else { "" } }}

# Rust coverage report, opened in the browser
coverage-html:
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --locked --html --open

# Documentation build check (warnings, including broken intra-doc links,
# treated as errors)
doc-check:
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi

# Unused-dependency check
machete:
    cargo machete

# Mutation testing sweep — slow, run on demand, not part of `just ci`
mutants:
    cargo mutants --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi

ts_src := "'packages/vite-plugin/src/**/*.ts' 'packages/vite-plugin/tests/**/*.ts' 'packages/vite-plugin/vitest.config.ts' 'packages/napi/*.d.ts' 'packages/cli/bin/**/*.js' 'apps/validate/src/**/*.ts'"
ts_src_only := "'packages/vite-plugin/src' 'packages/vite-plugin/vitest.config.ts' 'packages/napi/*.d.ts' 'packages/cli/bin/**/*.js' 'apps/validate/src'"
ts_tests_only := "'packages/vite-plugin/tests'"
md_src := "'**/*.md' '!node_modules/**' '!target/**' '!dist/**'"

# Lint and format check
lint:
    cargo fmt --check
    cargo clippy --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --locked -- -D warnings
    pnpm exec oxfmt --check {{ts_src}}
    pnpm exec oxfmt --check {{md_src}}
    pnpm exec oxlint {{ts_src_only}}
    pnpm exec oxlint -A pedantic -A perf -A style -A unicorn/consistent-function-scoping -A vitest/require-mock-type-parameters --vitest-plugin {{ts_tests_only}}

# Format code
fmt:
    cargo fmt
    pnpm exec oxfmt {{ts_src}}
    pnpm exec oxfmt {{md_src}}

# Check licenses, advisories, and banned crates
deny:
    cargo deny check

# Check for typos
typos:
    typos

# Lint GitHub Actions workflows for permission, credential, and supply-chain
# issues. --strict-collection fails on a workflow it cannot parse instead of
# skipping it, so a malformed file can never pass by being ignored.
zizmor:
    zizmor --offline --strict-collection .

# Everything the moon-managed pre-commit hook runs. `.moon/workspace.yml`
# calls this recipe rather than repeating the commands, so the hook and
# `just ci` can't drift apart.
pre-commit:
    cargo fmt --check
    cargo clippy --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --locked -- -D warnings
    typos
    cargo deny check

node = "~26"
pnpm = "11.27.1"
rust = "1.98.1"
moon = "2.4.5"

[plugins]
moon = "source:https://raw.githubusercontent.com/moonrepo/moon/master/proto-plugin.toml"

[settings]
auto-install = true
edition = "2021"
max_width = 120
use_small_heuristics = "Max"
msrv = "1.94"
too-many-arguments-threshold = 6
too-many-lines-threshold = 150
[files]
extend-exclude = ["apps/validate/baselines/"]

[default.extend-words]
# variable abbreviations used in pattern bindings
afe = "afe"
sme = "sme"
# ratatui is a real Rust TUI library
ratatui = "ratatui"
# beng is a real Unicode CLDR numbering-system identifier (Bengali)
beng = "beng"
[advisories]
version = 2
ignore = []

[licenses]
version = 2
allow = [
    "AGPL-3.0-or-later", # this workspace's own crates
    "MIT",
    "Apache-2.0",
    "Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception",
    "ISC",
    "BSD-2-Clause",
    "BSD-3-Clause",
    "Unicode-3.0",  # unicode-ident, unicode-id-start
    "Zlib",         # foldhash (via simd-json → oxc_resolver)
    "CC0-1.0",      # notify (via watchexec)
]

[bans]
multiple-versions = "warn"
# No skips: the duplicate oxc crate family these covered came in through
# oxc_module_lexer, which pinned 0.38.x against the main family's 0.135.x.
# That dependency is gone, and cargo-deny now reports every one of those
# skips as unnecessary.
skip = []

[sources]
unknown-registry = "deny"
unknown-git = "deny"
# https://moonrepo.dev/docs/config/workspace
$schema: "https://moonrepo.dev/schemas/workspace.json"

projects:
  core: "crates/core"
  cli: "crates/cli"
  cli-npm: "packages/cli"
  crates-binding: "crates/binding"
  napi: "packages/napi"
  validate: "apps/validate"
  vite-plugin: "packages/vite-plugin"

vcs:
  client: git
  defaultBranch: main
  sync: true
  hooks:
    pre-commit:
      - '. "$HOME/.cargo/env"'
      # Defined in the justfile so the hook and `just ci` share one definition.
      # Re-run `moon sync vcs-hooks` after changing this list.
      - "just pre-commit"

telemetry: false
# https://moonrepo.dev/docs/config/toolchain
#
# moon 2.0 renamed this file from `toolchain.yml` to `toolchains.yml`. Under
# the old name moon silently ignored it, so every version declared here was
# dead config -- which is why node/pnpm/rust versions live in `.prototools`
# and are inherited below rather than restated.
$schema: "https://moonrepo.dev/schemas/toolchains.json"

node:
  versionFromPrototools: true

pnpm:
  versionFromPrototools: true

rust:
  versionFromPrototools: true
  # proto is the single source of truth for the toolchain; moon must not
  # write a competing rust-toolchain.toml into the workspace.
  syncToolchainConfig: false
# List available commands
default:
    @just --list

# Install Cargo tools required for local development
install-tools:
    cargo install cargo-nextest --locked
    cargo install cargo-llvm-cov --locked
    cargo install cargo-machete --locked
    cargo install cargo-mutants --locked
    rustup component add llvm-tools-preview

# Check the public Rust API for accidental SemVer breaks against the last
# published version. Not wired into `just ci` yet — there is no published
# baseline to diff against until v0.1.0's first real crates.io release ships.
# Install with `cargo install cargo-semver-checks --locked` once needed.
check-api:
    cargo semver-checks check-release

# Install all dependencies
install:
    pnpm install
    cargo fetch

# Build all projects. Rust crates build via one workspace-wide cargo
# invocation, not `moon run :build` — that fans out one `cargo build -p`
# per crate, and every one of those processes contends for the same
# target/ file lock, serializing what moon's own scheduler thinks is
# parallel work (confirmed via `Blocking waiting for file lock` in verbose
# output). napi/vite-plugin have no such lock to contend over, so moon
# still orchestrates those directly.
build:
    cargo build --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi
    moon run napi:build vite-plugin:build
    cargo build --release

# Run all tests (Rust + TypeScript)
test: test-rust test-ts

# Run Rust tests (via nextest, which doesn't run doctests — paired
# with `cargo test --doc` to cover those too)
test-rust:
    cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --locked
    cargo test --doc --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi

# Run TypeScript tests
test-ts:
    pnpm --filter @oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin test

# Pack the npm packages and check napi arrives only as vite-plugin's transitive dependency (pm: npm or pnpm)
verify-install pm="pnpm":
    scripts/verify-install.sh {{ pm }}

# Run benchmarks
bench:
    cargo bench --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi

# Rust and TypeScript line coverage; with a threshold, fails if either is below it
coverage threshold="": (coverage-rust threshold) (coverage-ts threshold)

# Rust coverage: writes lcov.info and prints the summary before enforcing the threshold
coverage-rust threshold="":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --locked --lcov --output-path lcov.info
    cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only
    if [[ -n "{{ threshold }}" ]]; then
      cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only --fail-under-lines "{{ threshold }}"
    fi

# TypeScript coverage: prints the summary and writes packages/vite-plugin/coverage/lcov.info
coverage-ts threshold="":
    pnpm --filter @oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin exec vitest run --coverage {{ if threshold != "" { "--coverage.thresholds.lines=" + threshold } else { "" } }}

# Rust coverage report, opened in the browser
coverage-html:
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --locked --html --open

# Documentation build check (warnings, including broken intra-doc links,
# treated as errors)
doc-check:
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi

# Unused-dependency check
machete:
    cargo machete

# Mutation testing sweep — slow, run on demand, not part of `just ci`
mutants:
    cargo mutants --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi

ts_src := "'packages/vite-plugin/src/**/*.ts' 'packages/vite-plugin/tests/**/*.ts' 'packages/vite-plugin/vitest.config.ts' 'packages/napi/*.d.ts' 'packages/cli/bin/**/*.js' 'apps/validate/src/**/*.ts'"
ts_src_only := "'packages/vite-plugin/src' 'packages/vite-plugin/vitest.config.ts' 'packages/napi/*.d.ts' 'packages/cli/bin/**/*.js' 'apps/validate/src'"
ts_tests_only := "'packages/vite-plugin/tests'"
md_src := "'**/*.md' '!node_modules/**' '!target/**' '!dist/**'"

# Lint and format check
lint:
    cargo fmt --check
    cargo clippy --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --locked -- -D warnings
    pnpm exec oxfmt --check {{ts_src}}
    pnpm exec oxfmt --check {{md_src}}
    pnpm exec oxlint {{ts_src_only}}
    pnpm exec oxlint -A pedantic -A perf -A style -A unicorn/consistent-function-scoping -A vitest/require-mock-type-parameters --vitest-plugin {{ts_tests_only}}

# Format code
fmt:
    cargo fmt
    pnpm exec oxfmt {{ts_src}}
    pnpm exec oxfmt {{md_src}}

# Check licenses, advisories, and banned crates
deny:
    cargo deny check

# Check for typos
typos:
    typos

# Lint GitHub Actions workflows for permission, credential, and supply-chain
# issues. --strict-collection fails on a workflow it cannot parse instead of
# skipping it, so a malformed file can never pass by being ignored.
zizmor:
    zizmor --offline --strict-collection .

# Everything the moon-managed pre-commit hook runs. `.moon/workspace.yml`
# calls this recipe rather than repeating the commands, so the hook and
# `just ci` can't drift apart.
pre-commit:
    cargo fmt --check
    cargo clippy --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --locked -- -D warnings
    typos
    cargo deny check

# Everything the CI jobs run, minus the Node version matrix and verify-install
ci: lint test deny typos zizmor doc-check machete (coverage "90")

# Run moon compare task (accuracy vs react-docgen + react-docgen-typescript)
compare:
    moon run validate:compare

# Clean build artifacts
clean:
    moon clean
    cargo clean
    rm -rf node_modules

# Setup toolchain via proto
setup:
    proto install
    pnpm install
    moon sync vcs-hooks

# Run moon commands
moon *args:
    moon {{args}}

# Run cargo commands
cargo *args:
    cargo {{args}}

1	//! monokl's single unified error type and crate-wide `Result` alias.
2	//!
3	//! Per SPEC-001 (`.claude/specs/SPEC-001.json`), `MonoklError` is the crate's
4	//! sole error enum: every fallible `pub`/`pub(crate)` function in this crate
5	//! returns `crate::error::Result<T>` for its own `T`, with exactly one named
6	//! exception: `git_scope::blob_at_ref_in_repo`, a `pub(crate)` helper that
7	//! returns a bare `std::result::Result<String, String>` because it is always
8	//! mapped into `MonoklError::Git { operation: "show", .. }` at its sole call
9	//! site, `git_scope::blob_at_ref` (AC-003). `git_scope`, `persist`, and
10	//! `io_safety` are separate, not-yet-implemented tracks; this module defines
11	//! only the error contract they must conform to, not their bodies.
12	use camino::Utf8PathBuf;
13	
14	#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
15	#[cfg_attr(feature = "miette", derive(miette::Diagnostic))]
16	#[non_exhaustive]
17	pub enum MonoklError {
18	    // BLOCKED (AC-004, AC-001): the `Io(#[from] FileIoError)` variant this
19	    // spec requires cannot be added yet. FileIoError is owned by the
20	    // `io-errors` crate, which does not exist on disk at `../io-errors`
21	    // even though crates/monokl/Cargo.toml:43 already declares a
22	    // mandatory, non-optional dependency on it; that same dependency line
23	    // also pins `registry = "orin-cargo"`, and no `.cargo/config.toml`
24	    // `[registries.orin-cargo]` entry exists anywhere in this workspace
25	    // (the same AC-008B gap SPEC-004/PLAN-004 already documented). Until
26	    // both (a) an `io-errors` crate exists at `../io-errors` defining
27	    // `FileIoError`, and (b) `.cargo/config.toml` configures the
28	    // `orin-cargo` registry (or the dependency is repointed at a
29	    // resolvable source), this variant cannot be written without either
30	    // inventing an undocumented stub type or leaving the crate permanently
31	    // unbuildable. See this plan's blocker task (T-009) for the exact
32	    // decision needed.
33	    /// AC-005: three construction sites in the spec corpus --
34	    /// `text_search::search_files`, `WorkspaceIndex::build`'s walk, and
35	    /// `source_scan`'s per-directory walk -- in all three, `path` is the
36	    /// root of the walk in progress, not the failing entry.
37	    #[error("walker error at {path}")]
38	    Walk {
39	        path: Utf8PathBuf,
40	        #[source]
41	        source: ignore::Error,
42	    },
43	
44	    /// AC-006.
45	    #[error("regex compilation failed")]
46	    RegexBuild(#[from] grep_regex::Error),
47	
48	    /// AC-007: `path` is deliberately `std::path::PathBuf`, not
49	    /// `Utf8PathBuf` -- the entire point of this variant is that the path
50	    /// is not valid UTF-8, so it cannot be represented as camino's
51	    /// UTF-8-guaranteed type.
52	    #[error("non-UTF-8 path encountered: {path:?}")]
53	    NonUtf8Path { path: std::path::PathBuf },
54

61	    #[error("tokenizer init failed")]
62	    TokenizerInit,
63

65	    /// (1 site, `persist::load_cache`), cache-serialize (3 sites, all in
66	    /// `persist.rs`), CLI/output-serialize (4 sites: `output::render_json`,
67	    /// `output::render_json_compact`, `projection::project_inspect_result`,
68	    /// `projection::project_search_response`). Display text corrected from
69	    /// "json serialization failed" to the text below, since the
70	    /// cache-deserialize site is a parse failure the old text

72	    #[error("json parsing or serialization failed")]

126	    Git {
127	        operation: &'static str,
128	        message: String,
129	    },

You are working in the git worktree /Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/.claude/worktrees/sibling-conventions (a Rust workspace; one crate at crates/monokl). Edit ONLY files under crates/monokl/src/. Note: in this environment a shell hook rewrites `git` and `grep` through `rtk`; use `/usr/bin/git` and `/usr/bin/grep` (or the Grep tool) and `rtk proxy cargo ...` for cargo so output isn't filtered. Goal: bring the code in line with the conventions of the sibling repos (orin-dx/callisto and orin-dx/caliper), with NO behavior change. All 272 unit tests + 2 doctests currently pass with lints capped (`RUSTFLAGS="--cap-lints warn" cargo test --workspace --all-features`).

1. **Remove spec/criterion IDs and history from comments and doc comments.** Rule (from callisto AGENTS.md): code never cites spec or criterion IDs (SPEC-001, AC-007, T-009, PLAN-004, "this plan's", "this track", "per SPEC-xxx", "AC-021:" prefixes, etc.), and comments carry no history ("an earlier draft...", "corrected from...", "verified against cargo 1.96.0 in /tmp fixture", "was compiled and run..."). Caliper rules: comments only explain the non-obvious *why*, succinct, fill to 120 columns; doc comments follow RFC 1574 (first line one third-person sentence ending in a period, `///` for items, `//!` for modules, intra-doc links, backticks around code identifiers). Keep any genuinely useful *why* (e.g. why a path is std PathBuf not Utf8PathBuf; why Walk doesn't use source(); why a test exists) but say it in one or two plain sentences. Delete narration that just restates the code. Test names like `ac001_...` should be renamed to describe behavior (e.g. `michi_escape_value_deletes_newlines`). There are ~240 ID citations across error.rs, types.rs, query/*.rs, output/agent.rs, tests_types.rs, lib.rs — get them all (`/usr/bin/grep -rnE 'SPEC-[0-9]|AC-[0-9]|T-0[0-9]|PLAN-[0-9]|\bac[0-9]{3}' crates/` should return nothing at the end). Also remove references to `.claude/specs/...` paths in code.

2. **Make `rtk proxy cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` pass with zero errors.** About 340 currently: doc_markdown (mostly fixed by step 1 rewrites + backticks), `assertions_on_constants` (an assert on a const value — rewrite as a `const _: () = assert!(...)` compile-time assert, or drop it if the rewritten test still proves the same thing some other way; don't just delete coverage), `let_underscore_untyped` / `let_underscore_drop` (the workspace denies these: use `drop(x)` or a typed binding), `map_unwrap_or` (use `map_or`/`is_some_and`), `match_same_arms`, `needless_pass_by_value`, `float_cmp`, `extra_unused_lifetimes`/needless lifetimes, `too_many_lines` (limit is 150 via .clippy.toml; split tests if needed), `items_after_statements`, `redundant_closure_for_method_calls`, `range_plus_one`, `unreachable` (output/agent.rs walk_error_code: the three unreachable!() arms for WithLineNumber/WithPath/WithDepth — restructure so they're impossible without unreachable!, e.g. have innermost_walk_error and the classification be one recursive function that classifies wrapper variants by recursing, keeping exactly the same classification results; an existing commit previously added an allow for this — prefer a real fix, otherwise a narrowly-scoped `#[expect(clippy::unreachable, reason = "...")]`). Prefer real fixes over allows; any remaining `#[allow]` must be the narrowest scope with a `reason`, ideally `#[expect(..., reason = ...)]`. Do not touch the workspace Cargo.toml lint tables.

rust:
  syncToolchainConfig: false
projects: ["crates/*"]

vcs:
  defaultBranch: "main"

    pre-commit:
      - "just pre-commit"
    pre-push:
      - "just pre-push"
rust.yml
# NNNN. Short, decision-shaped title

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** YYYY-MM-DD

## Context

What forced this? The constraint, not the backstory. 2-4 sentences.

## Decision

What we're doing, stated plainly. A paragraph if it's one thing; a short paragraph plus bullets if it splits into a few discrete parts. Match the shape to the decision — don't pad a simple one or cram a multi-part one into a single block.

## Consequences

What this costs and what it buys. Bullets.

-
-

## Alternatives considered (optional)

Only if something else was a real contender. Name it and say why it lost — don't list every option that was never serious.
# Architecture Decision Records

Short, dated records of _architectural_ decisions — ones that shape system structure, boundaries, or contracts other code depends on. Not a changelog, not a design doc, not a place to explain what the code does — comments and `ARCHITECTURE.md` already do that.

## Index

One line per ADR, with what it guards. Add a line when you add an ADR.

- [1. Parse with OXC instead of the TypeScript compiler](0001-oxc-over-typescript-compiler.md) — do not add a type-checking pass to the default path. The opt-in backend is 0006.
- [2. Hand-write Serialize/Deserialize for PropType instead of deriving it](0002-manual-serialize-for-prop-type.md) — do not derive them on `PropType` or `CollectedType`.
- [3. Cache the DTS parse cache with positional (not named) MessagePack](0003-positional-msgpack-cache-encoding.md) — do not reorder, insert or remove `SourceData` fields without bumping `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION`.
- [4. Defer full type-checker integration](0004-defer-type-checker-integration.md) — superseded by 0006.
- [5. Contain panics at a single, per-item boundary](0005-panic-containment-boundary.md) — route anything reachable from a rayon `.map()`, a `DocgenPlugin` hook or a NAPI entry point through `contain_panic`.
- [6. Run the TypeScript backend as a second resolver](0006-semantic-backend-as-second-resolver.md) — do not patch `Opaque` leaves, give `crates/core` a compiler process or I/O, or route the backend through NAPI.


Changing any of these needs a new ADR.

## When to write one

Two gates, both required:

1. **Architectural.** It affects one of: system structure (module/crate boundaries, how components interact), a dependency or technology choice that ripples across the codebase, a data format or contract other code depends on, or a cross-cutting constraint (performance model, correctness discipline, security model).
2. **Expensive to reverse and not obvious from the code.** If it gets reverted in a year, what breaks, and would anyone know why?

If either answer is no, it's not an ADR.

Good candidates:

- Choosing OXC over the TypeScript compiler — a technology choice that shapes the whole extraction pipeline
- A serialization format with a hidden constraint (msgpack's positional encoding) — a data contract other code depends on
- Dropping a dependency, or an approach that was tried and abandoned

Not ADR material:

- A single function's algorithm choice, confined to that function — that's a code comment
- A bug fix — commit message, and if it's the kind of thing that could recur, a line in `rdt-coverage.md`
- A behavior-preserving refactor — commit message is enough
- A naming or style convention — that's `AGENTS.md` or a lint rule
- Anything already obvious from the code or from `AGENTS.md`'s non-negotiables
- Per-user preferences, workflow notes and tool quirks — that's agent memory

## Format

One file per decision: `docs/adr/NNNN-short-title.md`, numbered sequentially, never reused. Copy `0000-template.md` to start.

    cargo install cargo-nextest cargo-llvm-cov cargo-machete cargo-mutants cargo-deny typos-cli zizmor --locked
    rustup component add llvm-tools-preview

# Install the pinned toolchain and the moon-managed git hooks
setup:
    proto install
    moon sync vcs-hooks

# Build the workspace. One `cargo --workspace` invocation, not `moon run :build`: per-crate cargo processes all
# contend for the same target/ lock and serialize.
build:
    cargo build --workspace --locked

build-release:
    cargo build --workspace --release --locked

# Run tests with nextest, plus doctests, which nextest does not run
test:
    cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features --locked
    cargo test --doc --workspace --all-features --locked

# Line coverage; with a threshold, fails below it
coverage threshold="":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --all-features --locked --lcov --output-path lcov.info
    cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only
    if [[ -n "{{ threshold }}" ]]; then
      cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only --fail-under-lines "{{ threshold }}"
    fi

# Coverage report, opened in the browser
coverage-html:
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --all-features --locked --html --open

# Format check and clippy, with and without default features
lint:
    cargo fmt --all --check
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --no-default-features --locked -- -D warnings

# Clippy on the crates moon reports as affected, in one cargo invocation
lint-affected:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    projects=$(moon query projects --affected | jq -r '.projects[].id')
    if [ -z "$projects" ]; then exit 0; fi
    args=()
    for p in $projects; do args+=(-p "$p"); done
    cargo clippy "${args[@]}" --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings

fmt:
    cargo fmt --all

# Documentation build, with warnings (including broken intra-doc links) as errors
doc-check:
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --all-features --locked

# Licenses, advisories, bans and sources
deny:
    cargo deny check

# Unused dependencies
machete:
    cargo machete

typos:
    typos

# Workflow audit for permission, credential and supply-chain issues
zizmor:
    zizmor --offline --strict-collection .

# Mutation testing. Slow, so on demand only, not part of `just ci`.
mutants:
    cargo mutants --workspace

# Public API SemVer check against the last published version. Not in `just ci` until a first release exists.
check-api:
    cargo semver-checks check-release

clean:
    moon clean 2>/dev/null || true
    cargo clean

# Run by the moon-managed pre-commit hook
pre-commit:
    cargo fmt --all --check
    typos

# Run by the moon-managed pre-push hook
pre-push: pre-commit lint-affected

# Everything the CI jobs run
ci: lint test doc-check deny machete typos zizmor (coverage "90")

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
  RUST_BACKTRACE: 1

# Each job runs `just` recipes, so `just ci` locally does what CI does.
jobs:
  lint:
    name: Lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: rust
        run: echo "version=$(sed -n 's/^rust = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' .prototools)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.rust.outputs.version }}
          components: clippy,rustfmt
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@94c31af3204a9f15ab40b35ad084410b905bbc73 # v2.87.17
        with:
          tool: just,cargo-machete,typos
      - run: just lint doc-check machete typos

  test:
    name: Test / ${{ matrix.os }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: rust
        run: echo "version=$(sed -n 's/^rust = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' .prototools)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.rust.outputs.version }}
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@94c31af3204a9f15ab40b35ad084410b905bbc73 # v2.87.17
        with:
          tool: just,cargo-nextest
      - run: just test

  msrv:
    name: MSRV
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: msrv
        run: echo "version=$(sed -n 's/^rust-version = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' Cargo.toml)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.msrv.outputs.version }}
      - run: cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked

  coverage:
    name: Coverage
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: rust
        run: echo "version=$(sed -n 's/^rust = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' .prototools)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.rust.outputs.version }}
          components: llvm-tools-preview
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@94c31af3204a9f15ab40b35ad084410b905bbc73 # v2.87.17
        with:
          tool: just,cargo-nextest,cargo-llvm-cov
      - run: just coverage 90
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: coverage
          path: lcov.info
          retention-days: 14

  audit:
    name: Audit
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@94c31af3204a9f15ab40b35ad084410b905bbc73 # v2.87.17
        with:
          tool: just,cargo-deny,zizmor@1.29.0
      - run: just deny zizmor

  # The one check to require in branch protection.
  ci:
    name: CI
    needs: [lint, test, msrv, coverage, audit]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - if: contains(needs.*.result, 'failure') || contains(needs.*.result, 'cancelled')
        run: exit 1

# Grouped weekly updates, with security updates in their own group so an advisory fix is never hidden in a routine
# bump. The cooldown lets a yanked crate or pulled action release surface before it lands here.
version: 2

updates:
  - package-ecosystem: github-actions
    directory: /
    schedule:
      interval: weekly

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
  RUST_BACKTRACE: 1

# Each job runs `just` recipes, so `just ci` locally does what CI does.
jobs:
  lint:
    name: Lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: rust
        run: echo "version=$(sed -n 's/^rust = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' .prototools)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.rust.outputs.version }}
          components: clippy,rustfmt
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@94c31af3204a9f15ab40b35ad084410b905bbc73 # v2.87.17
        with:
          tool: just,cargo-machete,typos
      - run: just lint doc-check machete typos

  test:
    name: Test / ${{ matrix.os }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: rust
        run: echo "version=$(sed -n 's/^rust = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' .prototools)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.rust.outputs.version }}
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@94c31af3204a9f15ab40b35ad084410b905bbc73 # v2.87.17
        with:
          tool: just,cargo-nextest
      - run: just test

  msrv:
    name: MSRV
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: msrv
        run: echo "version=$(sed -n 's/^rust-version = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' Cargo.toml)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.msrv.outputs.version }}
      - run: cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked

  coverage:
    name: Coverage
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: rust
        run: echo "version=$(sed -n 's/^rust = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' .prototools)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.rust.outputs.version }}
          components: llvm-tools-preview
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@94c31af3204a9f15ab40b35ad084410b905bbc73 # v2.87.17
        with:
          tool: just,cargo-nextest,cargo-llvm-cov
      - run: just coverage 90
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: coverage
          path: lcov.info
          retention-days: 14

  audit:
    name: Audit
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@94c31af3204a9f15ab40b35ad084410b905bbc73 # v2.87.17
        with:
          tool: just,cargo-deny,zizmor@1.29.0
      - run: just deny zizmor

  # The one check to require in branch protection.
  ci:
    name: CI
    needs: [lint, test, msrv, coverage, audit]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - if: contains(needs.*.result, 'failure') || contains(needs.*.result, 'cancelled')
        run: exit 1

-    Session(SessionOwnership),  // held warm across many calls
-    Owned,     // monokl's host process spawns and fully owns this resource
-    Attached,  // discovers/attaches to a resource it doesn't control — must detect
-**Lifetimes nest** — an upgrader declares typed sub-resources, each with its own lifetime, not
-one flat field per impl. Canonical case: rust-analyzer's `proc-macro-srv-cli`, a subprocess
-loaded once and reused with crash-supervision, living *inside* an otherwise-`PerInvocation`
-Salsa build. C++ splits the other way: `ClangAstUpgrader{PerCall}` and `ClangdUpgrader{Session}`
-are two separate impls for one language, since one impl can't honestly carry two lifetimes.
-**Concurrency contract (invariant):** every `Session` resource is primed single-threaded before
-parallel readers (`par_iter` over files) touch it; LSP backends run behind a connection-actor
-(one task owns stdio, demultiplexes by request ID); `upgrade()` is read-only against the
-resource during the parallel phase. Covers in-process thread safety only, not cross-process
-Keyed by `ContentHash` (same key `FileAnalysis`'s disk cache uses) but a separate store with its
-own invalidation schedule, since confidence can change with no file change.
-    pub target: AnnotationTarget,       // pointer, not a copy
-    pub provenance: &'static str,       // same discipline as UpgradeOutcome.provenance
-    pub sentinel: Option<SentinelKind>, // which sentinel forced a downgrade, if any — §6
-    pub for_content: ContentHash,       // mismatch = "stale, discard", no further comparison
-pub enum AnnotationTarget { Span { start: usize, end: usize }, Symbol(SymbolId), Occurrence(OccurrenceId) }
-Three write paths accumulate into it: **eager** (inline during `analyze_with_profile`), **lazy**
-(query needs more precision than cached, backend now available), **retroactive** (future
-`monokl enrich` sweep). `compute_precision()` (§7) is pure and downgrade-only per annotation; it
-does not say what happens once several sit in the same `Vec` — gap #1.
-## Known gaps — genuinely unresolved, not merely undocumented
-findings #1–#4, #6 — no refutations recorded). Open questions for whoever writes spec@1:
-1. **No ledger reconciliation rule.** Writes accumulate as a `Vec<PrecisionAnnotation>` per
-   `ContentHash`, but nothing says how a reader resolves multiple entries on the same fact —
-   last-write-wins, min-precision-wins, dedup-and-replace, append-and-let-caller-choose are all
-   equally consistent with the struct as given.
-2. **No cross-process story for `Session(Owned)`.** The concurrency contract above covers
-   in-process thread safety only — nothing addresses an owned child process orphaned by `kill -9`
-   of the parent (no pidfile/lockfile/reaping), or two monokl invocations racing to own the same
-3. **No degrade-back-to-baseline contract for mid-session `upgrade()` failure.** Java (§8)
-   documents jdtls's hard-crash mode but mitigates it only at session *start* (a size gate) —
-   nothing covers the workspace crossing that threshold *after* the gate passes and crashing
-   mid-session. No fallback-to-cached-baseline, no re-establishment, no circuit-breaker.
-4. **No fallback for Kotlin/Scala with no JVM present.** C/C++ falls back to the tree-sitter tier
-   when Clang is missing; Kotlin/Scala were deliberately excluded from that same fallback tier, so
-   the JVM-subprocess analyzer is each language's only rung below the deferred `Exact` tier, with
-5. **No eviction or size-bound story for the ledger.** Combined with gap #1, growth is unbounded
-   on two axes (content hashes × entries per hash) for a long-running session or repeated
-   retroactive sweeps — no TTL, LRU, or max-size policy.
-## Why this file exists before implementation
-Two v0.1.0 decision points are shaped by this direction and should be checked against it now:
-  shared-envelope/per-language-variant pattern is what §4 reuses for `DaemonExtension`;
-  `FileAnalysis` needs a `daemon_extension: Option<DaemonExtension>` slot that stays `None` and
-  inert until a `PrecisionUpgrader` exists, never merged into `language_data`.
-- **`ContentHash` as a first-class, reusable type** (`cache-architecture.md`) — the ledger
-  indexes by the same `ContentHash` the disk cache computes, as a second, independently
-  invalidated store. If hash derivation stays buried inside the cache module instead of exposed
-  as its own type, the ledger can't reuse it without duplicating the hashing logic.

# oxc-react-docgen

10-100x faster than react-docgen-typescript. OXC parses TypeScript/TSX; we extract React component props and emit RDT-compatible JSON via `--format rdt`. See `docs/STATUS.md` for current state and known gaps.

## Commands

```bash
cargo test -p oxc-react-docgen-core          # unit + snapshot tests
cargo clippy -p oxc-react-docgen-core -- -D warnings
cargo build --release                         # full build including CLI
```

Or use `/check` and `/snapshot` for the common workflows.

## Non-negotiables

1. No `unwrap()` outside `#[cfg(test)]` — use `?`
2. `FxHashMap` for internal maps; `BTreeMap` for JSON-output maps
3. `CompactString` for type/prop names in hot paths
4. No AST refs escape `parse_file()` — allocator is local per call
5. No terminal/display code in `crates/core`
6. Always emit `Diagnostic` when degrading — never fail silently

## Architecture

```
OXC parse → SourceData (extractor/) → GlobalSourceData (pipeline/) → ComponentEntry (resolver/) → ExtractionOutput
```

No reverse dependencies. `pub(crate)` for implementation modules; `pub` only for consumer-facing API (`pipeline/`, `types/`, `react_types`).

See `ARCHITECTURE.md` for the full pipeline/crate-graph overview, and `docs/architecture/` for per-subsystem invariants and known gaps (pipeline orchestration, extractor, resolver, types, serialization, CLI, NAPI binding) — start at `docs/architecture/README.md`.

## Decisions

Read `docs/adr/README.md` before changing the parser choice, `PropType` serialization, the DTS cache format, panic containment or the semantic backend. Reversing an ADR needs a new ADR.

## Testing discipline

Two habits that repeatedly caught real bugs during the 2026-08-12 spec-validation pass (a stale-by-one-edit watch mode, always-zero watch stats — both had zero test coverage despite extensive existing suites):

1. **Sibling-path parity.** When a function parallels an already-tested one (e.g. `WatchSession::update_file` mirrors `extract()`'s resolve/panic-containment logic; `create_session`'s guard boundary mirrors `initialize_session`/`extract_file_incremental`'s), the new path needs a test asserting the _same_ contract, not just "it runs without error." A sibling path is exactly where coverage silently lapses.
2. **Assert content, not presence.** Prefer `assert_eq!` against an exact expected value over `contains(...)`/`is_some()`/liveness checks wherever the cost is comparable. A test asserting "component X exists" survives X's props resolving to stale or wrong data; a test asserting X's exact prop set does not.

## Crate guide

- `crates/core` — pure extraction logic; @crates/core/AGENTS.md
- `crates/cli` — clap CLI, no logic; @crates/cli/AGENTS.md
- `crates/binding` — thin NAPI wrapper, delegates to core

## Writing and commits

- Succinct: short sentences, bullets, tables. No backstory, hedging or filler. Banned words are in `docs/adr/README.md`.
- Never hard-wrap Markdown, commit messages or PR descriptions: one line per paragraph.
- Comments: only the non-obvious why, no history (the commit records it). Fill to 120 columns (`.rustfmt.toml`). Rewriting a comment block counts as writing it: re-fill and cut it, don't inherit the old wrapping.
- Commits: imperative subject, at most one or two sentences of why, no list of what changed, no "This commit...". Skip the body when the subject says it all.
---
name: rust-style
description: Apply when writing or modifying Rust code in this project.
---

**Goal:** Code correct by construction, readable under churn, performant in hot paths.

## Project-specific decisions

These are non-negotiables, not preferences:

- Internal maps: `FxHashMap`. JSON-output maps: `BTreeMap` (deterministic key ordering).
- Type/prop names: `CompactString` — avoids heap allocation for strings ≤24 bytes.
- No `unwrap()` outside `#[cfg(test)]` — use `?` and let callers decide what to do with failure.

## Control flow

`let...else` keeps the happy path flat:

```rust
let Some(entry) = map.get(key) else { return None };
let Ok(parsed) = input.parse::<u32>() else { continue };
```

## Matching

No wildcards — a compile error on unhandled variants is a feature:

```rust
match status { Status::Ok => .., Status::Err => .. }  // compiler tells you when Status grows
match status { Status::Ok => .., _ => .. }             // silently misses new variants
```

Full `match` over `matches!` for the same reason.

## Types

Newtypes when a bare type allows confusion. Enums when a bool parameter hides intent:

```rust
struct ScopedKey(CompactString);         // not: String
enum Visibility { Public, Private }      // not: is_public: bool
```

Explicit destructuring gets compiler errors when structs change:

```rust
let ComponentEntry { display_name, file_path, .. } = entry;
```

## Naming

Shadow variables through transformations — no `raw_`/`parsed_`/`trimmed_` prefixes:

```rust
let path = args.path;
let path = path.canonicalize()?;
let path = path.join("config.toml");
```

## Comments

Only when the WHY is non-obvious: a hidden constraint, a workaround, a non-obvious invariant. Not what the code does.
---
name: rust-types
description: Apply when defining new public structs or enums.
---

**Goal:** Every public type is immediately usable, visible in error messages, and extendable without semver breaks.

## Checklist before merging a new `pub struct` or `pub enum`

- `#[derive(Debug)]` — always
- `impl Display` — if it appears in messages, CLI output, or diagnostic text
- `impl std::error::Error` — if it represents a failure condition
- `impl AsRef<str>` — on string newtypes
- `#[non_exhaustive]` — on enums that will gain variants; adding one without this is a semver break
- `#[must_use]` — on functions whose return value the caller must not silently drop

## Wire or don't define

A new abstraction needs a real call site in the same PR — not a follow-up ticket. An unused type adds noise and false confidence. If the use case isn't clear yet, leave a note in the doc instead.

Read `docs/adr/README.md` before changing the parser choice, `PropType` serialization, the DTS cache format, panic containment or the semantic backend. Reversing an ADR needs a new ADR.

## Testing discipline

Two habits that repeatedly caught real bugs during the 2026-08-12 spec-validation pass (a stale-by-one-edit watch mode, always-zero watch stats — both had zero test coverage despite extensive existing suites):

1. **Sibling-path parity.** When a function parallels an already-tested one (e.g. `WatchSession::update_file` mirrors `extract()`'s resolve/panic-containment logic; `create_session`'s guard boundary mirrors `initialize_session`/`extract_file_incremental`'s), the new path needs a test asserting the _same_ contract, not just "it runs without error." A sibling path is exactly where coverage silently lapses.
2. **Assert content, not presence.** Prefer `assert_eq!` against an exact expected value over `contains(...)`/`is_some()`/liveness checks wherever the cost is comparable. A test asserting "component X exists" survives X's props resolving to stale or wrong data; a test asserting X's exact prop set does not.

## Crate guide

- `crates/core` — pure extraction logic; @crates/core/AGENTS.md
- `crates/cli` — clap CLI, no logic; @crates/cli/AGENTS.md
- `crates/binding` — thin NAPI wrapper, delegates to core

## Writing and commits

- Succinct: short sentences, bullets, tables. No backstory, hedging or filler. Banned words are in `docs/adr/README.md`.
- Never hard-wrap Markdown, commit messages or PR descriptions: one line per paragraph.
- Comments: only the non-obvious why, no history (the commit records it). Fill to 120 columns (`.rustfmt.toml`). Rewriting a comment block counts as writing it: re-fill and cut it, don't inherit the old wrapping.
- Commits: imperative subject, at most one or two sentences of why, no list of what changed, no "This commit...". Skip the body when the subject says it all.
---
name: rust-style
description: Apply when writing or modifying Rust code in this project.
---

**Goal:** Code correct by construction, readable under churn, performant in hot paths.

## Project-specific decisions

These are non-negotiables, not preferences:

- Internal maps: `FxHashMap`. JSON-output maps: `BTreeMap` (deterministic key ordering).
- Type/prop names: `CompactString` — avoids heap allocation for strings ≤24 bytes.
- No `unwrap()` outside `#[cfg(test)]` — use `?` and let callers decide what to do with failure.

## Control flow

`let...else` keeps the happy path flat:

```rust
let Some(entry) = map.get(key) else { return None };
let Ok(parsed) = input.parse::<u32>() else { continue };
```

## Matching

No wildcards — a compile error on unhandled variants is a feature:

```rust
match status { Status::Ok => .., Status::Err => .. }  // compiler tells you when Status grows
match status { Status::Ok => .., _ => .. }             // silently misses new variants
```

Full `match` over `matches!` for the same reason.

## Types

Newtypes when a bare type allows confusion. Enums when a bool parameter hides intent:

```rust
struct ScopedKey(CompactString);         // not: String
enum Visibility { Public, Private }      // not: is_public: bool
```

Explicit destructuring gets compiler errors when structs change:

```rust
let ComponentEntry { display_name, file_path, .. } = entry;
```

## Naming

Shadow variables through transformations — no `raw_`/`parsed_`/`trimmed_` prefixes:

```rust
let path = args.path;
let path = path.canonicalize()?;
let path = path.join("config.toml");
```

## Comments

Only when the WHY is non-obvious: a hidden constraint, a workaround, a non-obvious invariant. Not what the code does.
---
name: rust-types
description: Apply when defining new public structs or enums.
---

**Goal:** Every public type is immediately usable, visible in error messages, and extendable without semver breaks.

## Checklist before merging a new `pub struct` or `pub enum`

- `#[derive(Debug)]` — always
- `impl Display` — if it appears in messages, CLI output, or diagnostic text
- `impl std::error::Error` — if it represents a failure condition
- `impl AsRef<str>` — on string newtypes
- `#[non_exhaustive]` — on enums that will gain variants; adding one without this is a semver break
- `#[must_use]` — on functions whose return value the caller must not silently drop

## Wire or don't define

A new abstraction needs a real call site in the same PR — not a follow-up ticket. An unused type adds noise and false confidence. If the use case isn't clear yet, leave a note in the doc instead.

---
name: adr
description: Apply when an architectural decision was just made — one shaping system structure, boundaries, or a contract other code depends on — or when asked to write or review an Architecture Decision Record.
---

**Goal:** A future contributor (or you, in six months) understands why a hard-to-reverse architectural decision was made, in under a minute of reading.

## Decide if it's ADR material

Two gates, both required:

1. **Architectural** — it affects system structure (module/crate boundaries, how components interact), a dependency or technology choice that ripples across the codebase, a data format/contract other code depends on, or a cross-cutting constraint (performance model, correctness discipline, security model).
2. **Expensive to reverse and not obvious from the code** — if it gets reverted in a year, what breaks, and would anyone know why?

If either answer is no, skip it — it's a commit message, a code comment, or a line in `rdt-coverage.md`, not an ADR. A clever algorithm confined to one function, a naming convention, a behavior-preserving refactor: none of these are architectural even if someone spent real thought on them.

Unsure? Ask rather than guess — writing one nobody wanted is worse than skipping one that mattered.

## Write it

Full rules and voice guide: `docs/adr/README.md`. Template: `docs/adr/0000-template.md`. Read both before writing — don't rely on memory of them.

Find the next number by listing `docs/adr/*.md` and incrementing the highest. Copy the template, but treat its sections as a starting shape, not a form to fill mechanically — a one-paragraph decision doesn't need a forced "Alternatives considered" with nothing real in it. Cut sections that would just say "n/a."

Ground every claim in something checkable — a file, a line, a number, a test you actually ran. If you're about to write "this is faster" or "this was necessary," go verify it first (read the code, run the test, check git history) instead of asserting from a vague sense that it's probably true.

Don't hard-wrap paragraphs at a fixed column. One line per paragraph, let the editor soft-wrap — matches every other doc in this repo.

## Before you save it

Read it back once as the target contributor, not the author. Cut every sentence that would survive being deleted — check against `docs/adr/README.md`'s banned-word list and before/after table. If a section reads like a corporate template ("In conclusion, this represents..."), delete it; ADRs stop when the decision's been explained, they don't wrap up with a summary of themselves.

Short beats complete. If the technical depth genuinely doesn't fit on a screen, split it into its own doc and link it — see how `0004-defer-type-checker-integration.md` points at `docs/type-checker-integration.md` instead of inlining it.
Link types by name, not just backticks:

```rust
/// Returns [`ComponentEntry`], or `None` if resolution failed.
```

Add sections only when they carry information: `# Examples`, `# Panics`, `# Errors`, `# Safety`. Every public `fn` gets at least one example. Hide boilerplate with `# `:

````rust
/// # Examples
/// ```
/// # use oxc_react_docgen_core::pipeline::PipelineOptions;
/// let opts = PipelineOptions::default();
/// ```
````

American English spelling.

# 1. Keep FileIoError in monokl instead of a shared io-errors crate

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-10-21

## Context

The spec (`01-core-architecture.md` §1 and §27) puts `FileIoError` in a separate `io-errors` crate, pulled from a private `orin-cargo` registry. That crate was never written or published, and no `.cargo/config.toml` defines the registry, so `cargo metadata` failed at manifest parse and monokl could not build or run a single test.

## Decision

`FileIoError` is the `monokl::file_io` module, with the spec's §27 contents unchanged. `MonoklError::Io` wraps it with `#[error(transparent)]` and `#[from]`. There is no private registry: dependencies come from crates.io, or by pinned git revision from an `orin-dx` repository allowed in `deny.toml`.

## Consequences

- monokl builds and tests with no out-of-repo setup.
- Another orin-dx tool that wants the same type cannot depend on it without depending on monokl. When a second tool needs it, it moves to a shared crate, under michi's own "second independent data point" rule.
- `docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md` §1 and §27 still describe the separate crate and need a matching correction.

## Alternatives considered

- **A new michi crate.** michi renders agent-facing responses; its principles keep domain logic out, and a file I/O error with a path is domain logic. One consumer is also one data point, which michi's principles say is not enough to add a primitive.
- **`crates/io-errors` in this workspace.** It would be publishable on its own, but it adds a crate to version and release for one 70-line enum with one consumer. callisto merged its crates down to four for the same overhead.

# Architecture decision records

Short, dated records of architectural decisions: ones that shape system structure, boundaries, or contracts other code depends on. Not a changelog, not a design doc. Comments, `ARCHITECTURE.md` and `docs/architecture/` explain what the code does.

The spec's own decision log, [`docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md`](../spec/05-research-and-decisions.md), records how the spec was reached. ADRs record decisions made since, including any that depart from the spec.

## Index

One line per ADR, with what it guards. Add a line when you add an ADR.

- [1. Keep FileIoError in monokl instead of a shared io-errors crate](0001-file-io-error-lives-in-monokl.md): do not reintroduce a private registry; move `FileIoError` to a shared crate only when a second tool needs it.

Changing any of these needs a new ADR.

## When to write one

Two gates, both required:

1. **Architectural.** It affects system structure (module or crate boundaries, how components interact), a dependency or technology choice that ripples across the codebase, a data format or contract other code depends on, or a cross-cutting constraint (performance model, correctness discipline, security model).
2. **Expensive to reverse and not obvious from the code.** If it gets reverted in a year, what breaks, and would anyone know why?

If either answer is no, it's not an ADR. A single function's algorithm is a code comment; a bug fix or refactor is a commit message; a naming or style convention belongs in `AGENTS.md` or a lint.

## Format

One file per decision: `docs/adr/NNNN-short-title.md`, numbered sequentially, never reused. Copy `0000-template.md` to start.

- **Never edit history.** If a decision changes, write a new ADR and mark the old one's status `Superseded by NNNN`.
- **Status** is one of `Accepted`, `Superseded by NNNN`, `Deprecated`.
- Keep it to a screen. Put technical depth in `docs/architecture/` and link it.

## Writing it

Write it like you're explaining it to the next engineer over their shoulder. One line per paragraph, no hard wrapping. Sentence-case headers.

- Cut filler. If a sentence means the same without a word, delete the word.
- Banned by default: _leverage, utilize, robust, seamless, cutting-edge, essentially, basically, in order to, it's worth noting, it is important to note, at the end of the day._
- Concrete beats vague. Name the file, the number, the command.
- Active voice. "We chose X because Y."
- Show the trade-off. A decision with no downside is a fact, not a decision.

# Contributing

By participating in this project, you agree to abide by the [Code of Conduct](./CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). Found a security issue? See [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md) instead of opening a public issue.

## Where things stand

monokl is spec-stage — no `Cargo.toml`, no `src/`, nothing to build or run yet. The design is fully written up in [`docs/spec/`](docs/spec/README.md). If you're picking this up to start implementation, read [`docs/spec/README.md`](docs/spec/README.md) first; it tells you which file to read for which subsystem.

Before writing code against the spec, check [`docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md`](docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md) — it's the changelog for corrections made after the fact (compile-breaking gaps, dropped languages, adopted-but-unbuilt design changes). The other four spec files are the source of truth for _what_ to build; this one is the source of truth for _why_ it looks the way it does.

## Proposing a spec change

Don't silently edit around a design decision you disagree with. Add a dated entry to `docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md` explaining what changed and why — same discipline that's already been applied throughout that file. If the change is substantial enough to need its own writeup, add a new file under `docs/spec/` and link it from [`docs/spec/README.md`](docs/spec/README.md).

## Once there's code

These conventions are already locked into the spec — `docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md`'s workspace lint table — and apply from the first commit, not as an aspiration to grow into:

- **No `unwrap()`, `expect()`, `panic!()`, `unreachable!()`, or `unimplemented!()` in library code.** Denied at the workspace level via `clippy`. Fine in `#[cfg(test)]` code — assertions are supposed to panic on failure there.
- **`thiserror`, one error enum per crate**, composed via `#[from]`/`#[source]` rather than proliferating string-message variants. See `MonoklError` in [`docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md`](docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md) for the pattern.
- **Arena data never escapes a per-file parse call.** If you're touching a `LanguageAnalyzer` impl, everything in the returned `FileAnalysis` must be owned — no borrowed AST nodes, no lifetimes tied to the parser's allocator.
- **`camino::Utf8Path`/`Utf8PathBuf`**, not `std::path::Path` — the whole crate assumes UTF-8 paths.
- **`cargo nextest`** for running tests, **`insta`** for snapshot tests.

## Filing an issue

Say what you expected, what happened, and — if it's a spec-vs-reality mismatch — which file in `docs/spec/` you were reading. "The spec says X but Y happens" is more actionable than "this is broken."

# monokl

AST-aware code search for TypeScript, JavaScript and Rust, built for coding agents. Part of [Orin DX](https://orin-dx.com) (github.com/orin-dx). Agent-facing output goes through [michi](https://github.com/orin-dx/michi); don't hand-roll TOON lists, structured errors or hints that michi provides.

Vendor-neutral guidance. [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) adds Claude Code specifics.

## Read first

1. [`docs/spec/README.md`](docs/spec/README.md): which spec file covers what. The spec is the reconstruction source for unbuilt modules.
2. [`docs/architecture/README.md`](docs/architecture/README.md): which topic doc to read for the area you're changing.
3. [`docs/adr/README.md`](docs/adr/README.md) and [`docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md`](docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md): decisions already made. If something looks inconsistent, check here before "fixing" it.
4. [PRINCIPLES.md](PRINCIPLES.md): non-goals. No embedding reranker, no persistent trigram index, no tree-sitter TS/JS parser.

## Commands

```bash
just setup      # proto toolchain + moon git hooks
just ci         # everything CI runs
just test       # nextest + doctests
just lint       # fmt check + clippy, all features and no default features
```

Run one cargo command at a time; parallel cargo processes serialize on the `target/` lock. Never `git checkout Cargo.lock`.

## Current state

One crate, `crates/monokl`, with the error types, core data types, query language and michi output adapter. Modules are declared in `lib.rs` as they are implemented, not ahead of time, and a dependency is listed only once code uses it. [`.claude/plans/ACTIVE.md`](.claude/plans/ACTIVE.md) tracks what's next.

## Non-negotiables

- No `unwrap()`/`expect()`/`panic!()`/`unreachable!()`/`unimplemented!()` outside `#[cfg(test)]`. The workspace lint table denies them.
- One `thiserror` error enum, `MonoklError`. Compose failure modes with `#[from]`/`#[source]`; no `String`-message variant when a structured one is possible. File I/O failures are `FileIoError` ([ADR 0001](docs/adr/0001-file-io-error-lives-in-monokl.md)).
- `LanguageAnalyzer` implementations return fully owned data. No arena-borrowed AST node or parser-allocator lifetime in any field of `FileAnalysis`.
- `camino::Utf8Path`/`Utf8PathBuf` wherever a path appears.
- `FxHashMap`/`FxHashSet` for internal hot-path maps; `BTreeMap` for anything serialized, because output order must be deterministic.
- Core result types are not `Serialize`; wire shapes live in the output layer. See [`08-library-session-api.md`](docs/spec/08-library-session-api.md#9-plumbing-and-porcelain-two-crates).
- No caps or pre-rendered truncation strings in core. Counts only (`items_returned`/`items_total`); the output layer renders the marker.
- `unsafe_code` is denied workspace-wide.

## Rust style

Skills in [`.agents/skills/`](.agents/skills/) hold the detail: `rust-style` (control flow, matching, naming), `rust-types` (public type checklist, "wire or don't define"), `rustdoc` (doc comment format), `adr`.

- `pub(crate)` for implementation modules; `pub` only for the consumer API.
- No wildcard `_` arm on enums this crate owns; a compile error on a new variant is the point.
- Code never cites spec, criterion or plan IDs (`SPEC-001`, `AC-007`, `T-009`). Specs change; the code says what it guarantees in its own words, and tests name the behavior they prove.

## Testing

- `cargo nextest` plus `cargo test --doc`. `insta` for snapshots: accept a snapshot change only after confirming the new output is correct, not just different.
- Assert content, not presence: `assert_eq!` on the exact value over `contains`/`is_some`.
- Sibling-path parity: a function that mirrors an already-tested one gets a test asserting the same contract.
- CI gates line coverage at 90%.

## Fixing bugs

Look for structurally identical siblings and fix them in the same change. If one is deliberately left, say where and why.

When the spec itself is wrong, fix the spec file and add an entry to [`05-research-and-decisions.md`](docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md) explaining what was wrong and why the fix is right. A decision that departs from the spec with a credible alternative gets an ADR.

## Writing and commits

- Succinct: short sentences, bullets, tables. No backstory, hedging or filler. Banned words are in [`docs/adr/README.md`](docs/adr/README.md).
- Never hard-wrap Markdown, commit messages or PR descriptions.
- Comments explain only the non-obvious why, carry no history (the commit records it), and fill to 120 columns.
- Commits: Conventional Commits, imperative subject, at most one or two sentences of why. Skip the body when the subject says it all.

# Contributing

By participating in this project, you agree to abide by the [Code of Conduct](./CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). Found a security issue? See [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md) instead of opening a public issue.

## Setup

[proto](https://moonrepo.dev/proto) pins the toolchain in `.prototools`; [just](https://just.systems) runs every task.

```bash
just setup          # install the pinned Rust and moon, install git hooks
just install-tools  # nextest, llvm-cov, machete, mutants, deny, typos, zizmor
```

## Recipes

| Recipe | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `just ci` | Everything CI runs |
| `just test` | nextest plus doctests |
| `just lint` | `cargo fmt --check` and clippy with `-D warnings`, all features and no default features |
| `just doc-check` | `cargo doc` with warnings as errors |
| `just coverage 90` | Line coverage, failing below the threshold |
| `just deny` | Licenses, advisories, bans and sources |
| `just machete` | Unused dependencies |
| `just mutants` | Mutation testing, on demand only |

## Where things stand

One crate, `crates/monokl`, with the error types, core data types, query language and michi output adapter. The rest of the design is in [`docs/spec/`](docs/spec/README.md); start at its README. [`docs/architecture/`](docs/architecture/README.md) has topic docs per subsystem, and [`docs/adr/`](docs/adr/README.md) records decisions made since the spec.

## Proposing a change

- A spec correction: fix the spec file and add a dated entry to `docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md`.
- A decision with a credible alternative that is expensive to reverse: write an ADR (`docs/adr/0000-template.md`).
- Everything else: a PR with a Conventional Commits title.

Conventions are in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). Highlights: no `unwrap()`/`expect()`/`panic!()` outside tests, one `thiserror` error enum, owned data out of every parse, `camino` paths, 120-column formatting, and no spec IDs in code.

## Pull requests

- CI's aggregate `CI` check must pass: lint, tests on Linux and macOS, MSRV, 90% line coverage, and audit.
- Keep a PR to one topic.

## Filing an issue

Say what you expected, what happened, and, if it's a spec-vs-reality mismatch, which file in `docs/spec/` you were reading.

# Contributing

By participating in this project, you agree to abide by the [Code of Conduct](./CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). Found a security issue? See [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md) instead of opening a public issue.

## Setup

[proto](https://moonrepo.dev/proto) pins the toolchain in `.prototools`; [just](https://just.systems) runs every task.

```bash
just setup          # install the pinned Rust and moon, install git hooks
just install-tools  # nextest, llvm-cov, machete, mutants, deny, typos, zizmor
```

## Recipes

| Recipe | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `just ci` | Everything CI runs |
| `just test` | nextest plus doctests |
| `just lint` | `cargo fmt --check` and clippy with `-D warnings`, all features and no default features |
| `just doc-check` | `cargo doc` with warnings as errors |
| `just coverage 90` | Line coverage, failing below the threshold |
| `just deny` | Licenses, advisories, bans and sources |
| `just machete` | Unused dependencies |
| `just mutants` | Mutation testing, on demand only |

## Where things stand

One crate, `crates/monokl`, with the error types, core data types, query language and michi output adapter. The rest of the design is in [`docs/spec/`](docs/spec/README.md); start at its README. [`docs/architecture/`](docs/architecture/README.md) has topic docs per subsystem, and [`docs/adr/`](docs/adr/README.md) records decisions made since the spec.

## Proposing a change

- A spec correction: fix the spec file and add a dated entry to `docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md`.
- A decision with a credible alternative that is expensive to reverse: write an ADR (`docs/adr/0000-template.md`).
- Everything else: a PR with a Conventional Commits title.

Conventions are in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). Highlights: no `unwrap()`/`expect()`/`panic!()` outside tests, one `thiserror` error enum, owned data out of every parse, `camino` paths, 120-column formatting, and no spec IDs in code.

## Pull requests

- CI's aggregate `CI` check must pass: lint, tests on Linux and macOS, MSRV, 90% line coverage, and audit.
- Keep a PR to one topic.

## Filing an issue

Say what you expected, what happened, and, if it's a spec-vs-reality mismatch, which file in `docs/spec/` you were reading.

The embedder-side shape is an actor thread owning the `Workspace` by value with the current `Snapshot` published beside it, request-scoped `!Clone` snapshot leases, and a fixed pool of `min(available_parallelism(), 4)` — rust-analyzer (`config.rs:2784-2792`), `ty`, and `ruff` (`crates/ty/src/lib.rs:31-36`) all run analysis on a hand-rolled fixed pool with no async runtime beneath it, and there is no tokio anywhere in the ruff repository. `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` is rejected on tokio's own documentation: the pool defaults to 512 threads and is sized for I/O (`builder.rs:306`), its queue applies no backpressure (`builder.rs:544-549`), and a blocking task cannot be aborted so shutdown waits for an in-flight cold open (`blocking.rs:107-120`). From a non-rayon thread, `rayon_core::Registry::in_worker` injects the job and parks the caller on a latch contributing no work (`registry.rs:516-540`), so each concurrent call costs a parked thread plus the rayon pool's own. §3.2's unbounded stale-snapshot memory is therefore the embedder's bound, and it is `1 + pool_size`: five live revisions at a pool of 4, against 513 under a default blocking pool — 450–700 MB versus 46–72 GB at 50k files. §13's stale-snapshot benchmark now reports resident bytes per pinned revision so an embedder can multiply by its own bound, and the incremental benchmark uses a 28-op batch, the size a real briefing issues, rather than 10.

- **`types.rs`**: replaced every ID-laden doc with short item docs, keeping the non-obvious wire facts: internal vs adjacent tagging, the `Selff` rename, `Default` not applying when deserializing, the `bindings` default vs required `attributes`, non-finite scores becoming `null`, why `files` is a `BTreeMap`, and that `pub(super)` maps to `Module`. Several tests in `tests_types.rs` read this file's source, and they all still pass.
- **`query/mod.rs`, `query/lexer.rs`, `query/parser.rs`, `query/plan.rs`**:
  - Added module and item docs, including `# Errors` on `parse` and `# Panics` on `search_patterns`.
  - Rewrote the test comments as one-line reasons.
  - Changed constant `assert!`s on the trait-probe consts into `const { ... }` blocks inside the same `#[test]` functions, so the coverage is kept and checked at compile time.
  - Removed unused `'de` lifetimes, switched `map().unwrap_or()` to `map_or`, replaced `let _ =` with `drop(...)` or a typed binding, and changed `open..open + 1` to `open..=open`.
  - Renamed probe tests from `*_absence_*_pinned` to `*_has_no_*`.
- **`parser.rs` `content_to_term`**: replaced the duplicate `Token::RegexPrefix => None` / `_ => None` arms with one exhaustive `Token::RegexPrefix | Token::Plus | Token::Minus | Token::Eof => None`. The results are identical, and a new `Token` variant is now a compile error. I updated the structural test that pinned the arm to require `Token::RegexPrefix |` and no `_ =>` wildcard.
- **`output/agent.rs`**:
  - Added a module doc, docs for `ToonProjection`, `opt_cell`, `ToDomainError` and `render_projection` (with `# Errors`), and reworded the others.
  - Merged `innermost_walk_error` into a single recursive `walk_error_code`. It recurses on `WithLineNumber`, `WithPath`, `WithDepth` and a one-element `Partial`, then classifies the leaf with the same results as before. This removes all three `unreachable!()` calls and both `match_same_arms` allows. One of those allows had been attached to the wrong function, `io_error_code`.
  - `|e| e.monokl_code()` became `ToDomainError::monokl_code`.
  - Renamed tests away from `ac0xx_`/`b00x_` prefixes, for example `michi_escape_value_deletes_newlines`, `toon_validation_error_shape` and `walk_glob_maps_to_invalid_input`.
- **`tests_types.rs`**:
  - Replaced the long inventory and history docs with short `//` reasons.
  - Moved constant asserts into `const {}` blocks and turned four `float_cmp` checks into `to_bits()` equality, which is still exact.
  - Changed the `assert_shape(v: T)` helpers to take `&T` with merged arms, fixing `needless_pass_by_value` and `match_same_arms`.
  - Hoisted `fn assert_default` above the statements, replaced `let _ = ...` with typed bindings, `drop::<T>(...)` or `assert!(...is_ok())`, and removed an unused `'de`.

**Tests changed in `agent.rs` (count stays the same there)**
- `innermost_walk_error_partial_single_recurses` became `walk_error_code_partial_single_recurses`. It asserts `InvalidInput`, which can only come from the recursion.
- `innermost_walk_error_partial_non_single_does_not_recurse` would have duplicated `walk_error_code_partial_non_single_maps_to_external_failure`. I replaced it with a new case, `walk_error_code_partial_single_recurses_through_wrappers`: `Partial([WithPath(Io NotFound)])` must give `NotFound`.

This makes it build, brings it in line with callisto and caliper, and renames orin-axi to orin-dx.

## What changed
- **Build:** \`FileIoError\` is now \`monokl::file_io\` (spec §27 contents unchanged; ADR 0001). Only implemented modules and used dependencies are declared. michi is pinned to an FSL-1.1-MIT revision; the old pin was AGPL-3.0-or-later and cargo-deny rejects it.
- **Toolchain:** proto pins Rust 1.98.1 in \`.prototools\`; \`rust-toolchain.toml\` is gone. MSRV stays 1.96 and CI checks it.
- **Lints and format:** extra deny lints from both siblings, \`.rustfmt.toml\` at 120 columns, \`.clippy.toml\`, \`.typos.toml\`, stricter \`deny.toml\`.
- **CI:** \`.github/workflows/ci.yml\` with thin jobs that each run a \`just\` recipe: lint, tests on Linux and macOS, MSRV, 90% coverage gate, deny/zizmor, and an aggregate \`CI\` check. Plus dependabot.
- **Code:** no spec or criterion IDs in code; tests are named for behavior; clippy is clean under the workspace lints. No behavior change.
- **Docs:** AGENTS.md rewritten; \`.claude/semantic-model\` moved to \`docs/architecture\`; \`docs/adr\` added; rust-style, rust-types, rustdoc and adr skills added; decision-log entry §16 added in \`05-research-and-decisions.md\`.

## Verify
\`just ci\` passes locally: 273 tests plus 2 doctests, 98.6% line coverage. The MSRV job runs only in CI.

## Not in this PR
- Spec §1, §2, §27 and §28 still show the old manifest; §16 records the departure.
- \`.claude/specs\` and \`.claude/plans\` stay where they are.
- No changesets or \`callisto.toml\` yet.

3	**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-10-21
4	
5	## Context
6	
7	The spec (`01-core-architecture.md` §1 and §27) puts `FileIoError` in a separate `io-errors` crate, pulled from a private `orin-cargo` registry. That crate was never written or published, and no `.cargo/config.toml` defines the registry, so `cargo metadata` failed at manifest parse and monokl could not build or run a single test.
8	
9	## Decision
10	
11	`FileIoError` is the `monokl::file_io` module, with the spec's §27 contents unchanged. `MonoklError::Io` wraps it with `#[error(transparent)]` and `#[from]`. There is no private registry: every dependency, michi included (published as `michi-core`), comes from crates.io, and `deny.toml` denies any other source.
12	
13	## Consequences
14	
15	- monokl builds and tests with no out-of-repo setup.
16	- Another orin-dx tool that wants the same type cannot depend on it without depending on monokl. When a second tool needs it, it moves to a shared crate, under michi's own "second independent data point" rule.
17	- `docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md` §1 and §27 still describe the separate crate and need a matching correction.
18	
19	## Alternatives considered
