Yes. monokl now uses `michi-core` 0.3.1 from crates.io instead of a git pin, and `just ci` passes: 271 tests, lint, docs, deny, typos, zizmor, and 98.6% coverage. It's pushed to PR https://github.com/orin-dx/monokl/pull/3, and the PR description is updated.

- **Which crate:** only `michi-core` and `michi-pipeline` are on crates.io. The `michi` name there still belongs to an unrelated project, and the old `michi-toon` and similar crates are now folded into `michi-core`. In `Cargo.toml` I renamed it back to `michi`, so none of monokl's `michi::` paths had to change.
- **No more git sources:** `deny.toml` no longer needs an exception for a git dependency, so anything not from crates.io is now rejected.

**Changes from michi 0.3:**
- **Newline escaping is fixed.** The old michi deleted newlines, which is item A1 in `MICHI-ADJUSTMENTS.md`, and monokl's `cell()` escaped them as a workaround. michi 0.3 escapes them itself, so keeping the workaround would have escaped twice and shown agents a literal `\n` instead of a line break. `cell()` now passes text through unchanged.
- **Null and empty values now look different.** A missing value renders as `null` and an empty string as `""`.
- **A single hint renders on one line**, as `help[1]: …`.
- **Commas in field names are now quoted instead of rejected.** I changed the validation test to use a duplicate field name, which michi still rejects.

The `MICHI-ADJUSTMENTS.md` file in your main checkout may now be out of date. michi's tests suggest A1 and A2 are both fixed in 0.3.

The sandbox blocked some steps here: cargo writing its download cache, the cargo-deny database lock, gpg commit signing, and `gh`'s TLS connection. I reran those outside it. The commit is signed with your key. You can adjust these restrictions with `/sandbox`.

53	### A3. `render_toon`'s row/header arity mismatch is a `debug_assert!`, not a handled error
54	
55	`crates/michi-toon/src/render.rs:142` — a row whose length doesn't match the header count
56	panics in debug builds via `debug_assert!`, silently mismatches in release. For a library
57	meant to be embedded in multiple production CLI/agent tools, a panic path reachable from
58	malformed-but-plausible caller input (not just programmer error) is a rough edge —
59	monokl's own adapter design works around this with a const-generic trait that makes arity
60	a compile-time guarantee, but that's a caller-side mitigation, not a library-level fix.
61	Worth considering whether `render_toon` should return `Result` (or call `.validate()`
62	internally) instead of trusting the caller to have gotten arity right.
63	
64	### A4. `AgentResponse::toon_body()` swallows `validate()` failure into the body, with `is_error: false`
65	
66	If `ToonOptions::validate()` fails, the failure text gets written into the *body* of an
67	otherwise-successful-looking response (`isError: false`, `exit_code` unset/0). An agent
68	consuming this sees a normal-looking success response whose content happens to be an
69	error message — worse than a normal error, since nothing signals "don't trust this
70	payload." Either call `.validate()` automatically before rendering and surface real
71	failures as real errors, or make this failure mode visible in `is_error`.
72	
73	### A5. `DomainError::render()`/`render_hints`/`append_hints` don't sanitize newlines
74	
75	Unlike the TOON path, `error.rs`'s `render()` and `hints.rs`'s `append_hints` write
76	`message`/hint text raw into a line-oriented `key: value` / `help[N]:` block. A message or
77	hint containing a newline (e.g. relaying multi-line subprocess stderr, which is common —
78	git, a linter, a compiler) produces a malformed, unparseable block: an orphan line with no
79	`key:` prefix. Verified live:
80	```
81	error: external_failure
82	message: git_failed: git rev-parse failed: fatal: ambiguous argument 'nope'
83	Use '--' to separate paths          ← orphan line, breaks any KV parser
84	exit_code: 1
85	```
86	Same class of bug as A1, in a different module — worth a single shared sanitization pass
87	applied consistently across every render path, not just TOON's.
88	
89	---
90	
91	## Category B — already michi's own stated direction, monokl ready to be the evidence
92	
93	Not new asks. `PRINCIPLES.md`'s own "split the decision from the signal" section already
94	designs this and flags it explicitly as **not yet implemented**:
95	
96	```rust
97	pub struct TruncationOutcome<T> { pub kept: Vec<T>, pub total_before: usize, pub truncated: bool }
98	pub fn truncate_by_count<T>(items: Vec<T>, max: usize) -> TruncationOutcome<T>;
99	pub fn truncate_by_bytes<T>(items: Vec<T>, max_bytes: usize, size_of: impl Fn(&T) -> usize) -> TruncationOutcome<T>;
100	```
101	
102	monokl's own `budget.rs` (spec'd, not yet implemented) needs exactly this shape: cap a
103	`Vec<RankedBlock>` by a size metric and report what got cut, in a consistent agent-
104	readable form. The one difference is the metric — monokl caps by **LLM token count**
105	(tiktoken/o200k_base), not byte length. But `size_of: impl Fn(&T) -> usize` already
106	accepts *any* caller-supplied sizing function — feed it a token-counting closure and
107	`truncate_by_bytes` (or a `truncate_by_size`/generically-named variant) already covers
108	monokl's case with zero new michi surface. monokl isn't asking for something new here —
109	it's offering to be the real-consumer evidence this sketch has been waiting for.
110	
111	---
112	
113	## Category C — genuinely cross-tool ergonomic gap, not proven by monokl alone but structurally likely to recur
114	
115	### C1. No helper for building a `DomainError` from a `thiserror`-based domain error while preserving its cause chain
116	
117	`DomainError`'s `impl std::error::Error for DomainError {}` is empty — `source()` returns
118	`None` unconditionally, and thiserror's `Display` doesn't include `#[source]` either. So
119	any consumer converting their own crate's `thiserror` enum (the shape monokl's own
120	`AGENTS.md` mandates — "one thiserror error enum per crate" — and plausibly true of every
121	other orin-axi tool too, if they follow the same convention) into a `DomainError` has to
122	manually walk `Error::source()` themselves to avoid silently dropping the cause chain.
123	monokl's adapter had to write this from scratch:
124	
125	```rust
126	fn chain_lines(e: &dyn std::error::Error) -> Vec<String> { /* walk .source(), one line per link */ }
127	```
128	
129	This isn't monokl-specific — it's the generic shape of "I have a thiserror enum, I want a
130	`DomainError` that doesn't lose the cause chain," which is plausibly every consumer's
131	first integration step. Unlike the `ErrorCode` question below, this doesn't require
132	michi to know anything about monokl's domain — it's a pure mechanical utility
133	(`DomainError::from_error_chain(e: &dyn std::error::Error, code: ErrorCode) -> Self`, or
134	similar) that would generalize immediately. Flagging this as the strongest Category-C
135	candidate — closer to Category A than a "maybe" in spirit, since it doesn't require any
136	domain knowledge to justify, just recognizing the chain-loss gap generically.
137	
138	---
139	
140	## Category D — flagged, explicitly NOT a proposal: doesn't clear gate 3 yet
141	
142	### D1. `ErrorCode`'s fixed 9 variants can't cleanly represent all of monokl's error shapes
143	
144	Mapping monokl's 14-variant `MonoklError` onto `ErrorCode` (`InvalidInput | NotFound |
145	Unauthorized | Forbidden | Conflict | RateLimited | Unavailable | Timeout |
146	ExternalFailure`): 6 map cleanly, 3 need per-variant judgment calls, 5 (`TokenizerInit`,
147	`Json`, `LockPoisoned`, plus two others) get forced into `ExternalFailure` despite being
148	internal-invariant-violation shaped, not "a downstream dependency failed" shaped.
149	
150	**This is explicitly not a proposal to add `ErrorCode::Internal`.** Tracing
151	`Error::class()` shows the retry semantics already resolve correctly (it checks
152	`retryable` before falling back to `default_class()`, so an adapter calling
153	`.retryable(false)` on those five variants correctly yields `ErrorClass::Internal` even
154	though the *label* stays `"external_failure"`). The residual gap is purely label
155	granularity for agent legibility, and monokl's own adapter design already mitigates it
156	(a `monokl_code()` message-prefix carrying the finer distinction). Per gate 3, this is
157	one data point — worth having in mind, not worth building on monokl's evidence alone.
158	If it turns out Firkin, Lumen, or Pulse independently hit the same "internal bug vs.
159	external failure" ambiguity, that's the second data point that would actually clear the
160	bar — flagging now so it's not forgotten if that confirmation shows up later.
161	
162	---

167	  `error.rs`/`hints.rs`'s render paths (same bug, two places); `toon::list()`'s

171	  build `TruncationOutcome<T>`/`truncate_by_bytes` (or a size-generic variant) — it's
172	  already sketched in `PRINCIPLES.md`, just not implemented yet.
173	- **Worth adding, generalizes on its own merits**: a chain-preserving
174	  `DomainError::from_error_chain()` constructor for thiserror-based domain errors.
175	- **Explicitly not proposing**: new `ErrorCode` variants. One tool's evidence isn't

15-- One established exception: char/byte-level truncation (`truncate`, `ToonOptions::max_cell_len`) — treated as rendering safety, not business logic.
16:- **The ceiling:** if a tool's real need is more sophisticated than a generic primitive can serve — a custom ranking algorithm, a heuristic tuned to one tool's data shape — that's a sign the primitive doesn't belong in michi, not a sign to make michi's primitive more complex. See [Split the decision from the signal](#split-the-decision-from-the-signal) for how to resolve this without compromising on either.
17-
18-### 2. Small default dependency set
19-
20-The default build depends only on `thiserror` and `compact_str`. Anything else is opt-in behind a Cargo feature.
21-
22-- Adding a mandatory dependency needs a recorded decision in `docs/spec/06-decisions.md`. Prefer caller-supplied injection (a closure, a trait) first.
23-
24-### 3. Genuinely cross-tool — verified, not assumed
25-
26-Earns inclusion when independent, real tools would otherwise hand-roll the identical pattern.
27-
28-- "Independent" and "real" are load-bearing. One tool using a pattern heavily is one data point, not proof.
29-- **What clearing this bar looks like:** a survey across several real agent-facing dev tools (a code-search engine, a CLI proxy, a context-compression tool, a code-graph server) found `help[]`-shaped "note for the agent" hints independently reinvented, inconsistently, in every one of them.
30-- A pattern seen in only one tool — however heavily repeated inside that tool — isn't there yet. Watch for a second independent confirmation before building it.
31-
32-### 4. Doesn't duplicate an existing primitive
33-
34-Check `hints` / `recovery` / `idempotency` / `status` / `error` / `mcp` first. Verify the distinction concretely — don't assume novelty from a vibe.
35-
36-- "This looks similar to X" means go read X's source, not assume it's covered.
37-- Example: a proposed "diagnostics" primitive looked adjacent to `idempotency::PartialSuccess` — until actually reading `PartialSuccess`'s doc comment showed it's scoped to multi-step _mutating_ operations, not read-path degradation. They turned out genuinely distinct, but that took checking, not assuming either way.
38-
39-### 5. Deviations get tracked, not silently absorbed
40-
41-Where the final shape diverges from the original ask or an earlier draft, it goes in a Design Decisions table. Spec and code should never quietly drift apart.
42-
43----
44-
45:## Split the decision from the signal
46-
47-Gate 1's ceiling ("stay generic" vs. "real tools need real sophistication") isn't a tension to compromise on — it's usually an architecture problem. Separate the _domain-specific decision_ from the _universal signal_.
48-
49-**Worked example: truncation.** Deciding _which_ items survive a budget is tool-specific — personalized-PageRank over a call graph, a statistical outlier-preserving sampler, a simple first-N cutoff. None of that belongs in michi. But _reporting_ what got cut, in a consistent agent-readable shape, is exactly what every tool needs regardless of how it decided:
50-
51-```rust
52-/// What survived some truncation/budget decision, however it was made.
53-pub struct TruncationOutcome<T> {
54-    pub kept: Vec<T>,
55-    pub total_before: usize,
56-    pub truncated: bool,
57-}
58-
59-impl<T> TruncationOutcome<T> {
60-    /// Michi's standard help[]-shaped signal for what got cut — same
61-    /// contract regardless of which strategy produced this outcome.
62-    pub fn hint(&self, guidance: impl Into<String>) -> Option<Hint> { /* ... */ }
63-}
64-
65-// "Best practice" strategies michi ships, with no extra dependencies, for the common case:
66-pub fn truncate_by_count<T>(items: Vec<T>, max: usize) -> TruncationOutcome<T>;
67-pub fn truncate_by_bytes<T>(items: Vec<T>, max_bytes: usize, size_of: impl Fn(&T) -> usize) -> TruncationOutcome<T>;
68-```
69-
70-A caller with a genuinely novel heuristic never has to fit their algorithm into michi's shape — they wrap whatever they decided in `TruncationOutcome` and get the same hint/report format everyone else gets. Michi owns the contract, not the heuristic.
71-
72-**When a new primitive seems too domain-specific to generalize, ask whether it splits this way first.** Often only half of it actually is.
73-
74----
75-
76-## How work gets done
77-
78-Heuristics, not hard rules — process needs contextual judgment the content checklist doesn't.
79-
80-### 1. TDD, always
81-
82-Failing test first, verified red for the right reason, then implementation, then green. No implementation code without a preceding red test.
83-
84-### 2. Independent verification before "done"

31:/// Number of decimal digits in `n`.
41:/// Truncate `content` to at most `max_chars` Unicode scalar values, appending an agent-readable suffix when
42:/// truncation occurs.
43:///
44:/// The suffix is `" ({removed} more chars — use {hint})"`, where `removed` is the number of chars cut (the input's
45:/// char count minus the chars kept, not the original length). The `— use {hint}` clause is the caller's instruction:
46:/// michi never invents one, and an empty `hint` drops the clause, giving `" ({removed} more chars)"`. The whole
47:/// result, suffix included, never exceeds `max_chars` chars, and as many chars as fit are kept.
48:///
49:/// When `max_chars` cannot hold the full suffix plus at least one kept char, the result is instead the first
50:/// `max_chars - 1` chars followed by `…` (just `…` for `max_chars == 1`, and the empty string for `max_chars == 0`),
51:/// never a fragment of the suffix.
52:///
53:/// Uses char boundaries — never splits a Unicode scalar. Returns the original string unchanged when
54:/// `content.chars().count() <= max_chars`.

Both open items are worth building, and both are small. B (truncation reporting) is the stronger case: michi's own `PRINCIPLES.md` already sketches the API, and caliper has hand-rolled the same signal. C1 (keeping an error's cause chain) is a mechanical helper, but so far only monokl has needed it.

## B. `TruncationOutcome`: report what got cut, however it was cut

**Problem.** Every tool that caps a list decides for itself which items survive. Telling the agent what was dropped is a separate job, and right now each tool does it its own way:
- monokl's spec (Part 8 §9.1, `08-library-session-api.md:487`) has core report `items_returned` and `items_total`, and leaves the output layer to render the "there is more" signal.
- caliper hand-rolls a `"...(+N)"` marker (`truncate_with_indicator`, `caliper/crates/core/src/toon.rs:97`).

That's two independent tools inventing the same signal, which is the evidence `PRINCIPLES.md` gate 3 asks for. Say so in the PR.

**Current michi state.**
- `PRINCIPLES.md:45-70` ("Split the decision from the signal") sketches this API, but it isn't implemented.
- `truncate.rs` only truncates within a string (`truncate`, `truncate_inline`), not lists.
- `AgentResponse` and `ToonOptions` already have `total_count`, which renders `totalCount: N`. That covers half the signal.

**Proposed API.** This is the sketch from `PRINCIPLES.md`, with three changes:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct TruncationOutcome<T> {
    pub kept: Vec<T>,
    pub total_before: usize,
}

impl<T> TruncationOutcome<T> {
    /// For callers with their own selection heuristic: wrap whatever they kept.
    pub fn new(kept: Vec<T>, total_before: usize) -> Self;
    pub fn truncated(&self) -> bool { self.kept.len() < self.total_before }
    pub fn omitted(&self) -> usize;
    /// `None` when nothing was cut.
    pub fn hint(&self, guidance: impl Into<String>) -> Option<Hint>;
}

pub fn truncate_by_count<T>(items: Vec<T>, max: usize) -> TruncationOutcome<T>;
pub fn truncate_by_size<T>(items: Vec<T>, budget: usize, size_of: impl Fn(&T) -> usize) -> TruncationOutcome<T>;
```

The three changes:
1. **`truncated` is a method, not a field.** A stored `bool` can disagree with `kept.len()` and `total_before`.
2. **There's a `new()` constructor.** `#[non_exhaustive]` stops other crates from building the struct by hand. Without `new()`, a tool with its own heuristic, which is the whole point of the type, couldn't create one.
3. **`truncate_by_size` replaces `truncate_by_bytes`.** `size_of` can measure anything, and monokl's budget is tokens, not bytes.

**Decisions to make (record them in michi's Design Decisions table):**
- **How `truncate_by_size` fills the budget.**
  - *Stop at the first item that doesn't fit:* keeps order, and the rule is easy to explain.
  - *Skip items that don't fit and keep going:* fills the budget more completely, but output order no longer says what was dropped.
  - I'd stop at the first item that doesn't fit; a tool that wants the other behavior uses `new()`.
- **A first item larger than the budget.** Either `kept` is empty with `truncated() == true`, or the first item is always kept. I'd return empty and let the hint explain why.
- **Hint wording.** Something like `showing {kept} of {total}; {guidance}`, with the `guidance` text left to the caller, the same way `truncate` handles its hint. This keeps michi from inventing a flag the calling tool might not have.
- **Wiring into `AgentResponse`.** A `.truncation(&outcome, guidance)` builder that sets `total_count` and appends the hint would keep the two from drifting apart. Check gate 4 first: it overlaps the existing `total_count` field, and that overlap is the reason to have one call set both.

**Tests to write first (michi works test-first):**
- Empty input, zero cap and an exact fit: nothing is cut and `hint()` returns `None`.
- `truncate_by_count` keeps the first N items, in order.
- `truncate_by_size` stops at the first item that doesn't fit, including the oversized-first-item case.
- `size_of` additions saturate rather than overflowing.
- `hint()` produces exact text, checked against string literals.
- `new(kept, total)` for a custom heuristic renders the same hint as the built-in functions.

**How monokl would use it:** the future `budget.rs` would wrap its token-capped `Vec<RankedBlock>` in a `TruncationOutcome`. The output layer would render it, replacing the pre-rendered `truncation_marker` strings that the spec bans from core.

## C1. Keep an error's cause chain when building a `DomainError`

**Problem.** `DomainError` implements the `Error` trait, but `source()` always returns `None` (`error.rs:272`). There's no way to build one from a `thiserror` error without manually walking the `source()` chain. Every consumer that follows the orin-dx "one thiserror enum" rule has to write that loop. monokl did, in `to_domain_error` (`crates/monokl/src/output/agent.rs:638-647`):
1. `message` = the error's own `Display`.
2. Walk `source()` and add each link's `Display` as a hint.
3. Split each link on line breaks (`split_display_lines`, line 680).

**Current michi state.**
- `DomainError` derives `Clone` and, behind a feature flag, `schemars::JsonSchema`.
- `render()` now escapes messages and hints per TOON 4.4. So the line-splitting in step 3 is no longer required for correct output, only a formatting preference.

**Proposed API:**

```rust
impl DomainError {
    /// `message` is `err`'s own Display; each `source()` link's Display becomes a hint, outermost first.
    pub fn from_error(code: ErrorCode, err: &(dyn std::error::Error + 'static)) -> Self;
}
```

**Decisions to make:**
- **Should `source()` work in Rust code too?**
  - **Render-only (the API above):** no new field. The chain survives only in rendered output (the hints).
  - **Also store the cause:** add `source: Option<Arc<dyn Error + Send + Sync>>`. `Arc` keeps `DomainError` cloneable, and `source()` then works for code using it as a Rust error.
    - Costs: it needs `#[schemars(skip)]`, the `Send + Sync` checks in michi-core's `lib.rs` tests need re-checking, and the error constructor needs an owned error (`impl Error + Send + Sync + 'static`).
  - **My recommendation:** ship render-only first. Add the stored cause only when a consumer needs `source()`.
- **Hint per chain link or per line.** monokl does one hint per line. Now that michi escapes line breaks, one hint per link is simpler and loses nothing. Pick one and document it.
- **Message prefix.** monokl prefixes the message with its own code (`walk: …`). Leave that to callers (`from_error(...)`, then edit `.message`), not a parameter.
- **Gate 3 evidence is thin.** Only monokl has hand-written this. callisto and caliper use miette's `#[diagnostic(transparent)]` and don't use michi. If you'd rather not build on one data point, the PR can say this is a mechanical helper with no domain knowledge in it. That was the argument in `MICHI-ADJUSTMENTS.md`, but it's weaker than B's evidence.

**Tests to write first:**
- A two-level `thiserror` chain gives the exact message plus exactly one hint per cause, outermost first.
- An error with no source gives no hints.
- A multi-line cause renders as a single escaped hint.
- With the miette feature on, `help()` includes the chain.

**How monokl would use it:** most of `to_domain_error` collapses to `DomainError::from_error(code, self)` plus monokl's code prefix and recovery hints. `split_display_lines` can then go.

---

Once both ship, delete `MICHI-ADJUSTMENTS.md`; its A items are already fixed in michi 0.3.1. I can file B and C1 as issues on orin-dx/michi with this text if you want them tracked there.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct TruncationOutcome<T> {
    pub kept: Vec<T>,
    pub total_before: usize,
}

impl<T> TruncationOutcome<T> {
    /// For callers with their own selection heuristic: wrap whatever they kept.
    pub fn new(kept: Vec<T>, total_before: usize) -> Self;
    pub fn truncated(&self) -> bool; // kept.len() < total_before
    pub fn omitted(&self) -> usize;
    /// `None` when nothing was cut.
    pub fn hint(&self, guidance: impl Into<String>) -> Option<Hint>;
}

pub fn truncate_by_count<T>(items: Vec<T>, max: usize) -> TruncationOutcome<T>;
pub fn truncate_by_size<T>(items: Vec<T>, budget: usize, size_of: impl Fn(&T) -> usize) -> TruncationOutcome<T>;
```

This departs from the `PRINCIPLES.md` sketch in three ways. Record each one:

1. `truncated` is a method, not a stored `bool`, so it can never disagree with `kept.len()` and `total_before`.
2. `new()` exists. Because the struct is `#[non_exhaustive]`, a caller outside the crate cannot build it any other way, and wrapping a custom heuristic is the whole point.
3. The function is `truncate_by_size`, not `truncate_by_bytes`. `size_of` is caller-supplied, and monokl measures tokens, not bytes.

### Decisions to make

- **How `truncate_by_size` fills the budget.** Stopping at the first item that does not fit keeps order and is easy to explain. Skipping it and continuing fills the budget better, but the output order no longer says what was dropped. Recommendation: stop at the first item that doesn't fit. A tool that wants the other behavior uses `new()`.
- **A first item larger than the whole budget.** Recommendation: `kept` is empty and `truncated()` is true. The hint explains why.
- **Hint wording.** For example `showing {kept} of {total_before}; {guidance}`. `guidance` is the caller's instruction, as with `truncate`'s hint: michi never invents a flag the calling tool may not have.
- **`AgentResponse` integration.** Consider a `.truncation(&outcome, guidance)` builder that sets `total_count` and appends the hint, so the two can't disagree. Check gate 4 against the existing `total_count` first; that overlap is the reason to have one call set both.
- **Module.** `truncate.rs`, or a new module if list-level and string-level truncation read better apart.

### Tests to write first

- Empty input, a cap of zero, and an exact fit: nothing is cut, and `hint()` returns `None`.
- `truncate_by_count` keeps the first N items, in order.
- `truncate_by_size` stops at the first overflow, including the oversized-first-item case.
- `size_of` accumulation saturates instead of overflowing.
- `hint()` text matches exact string literals.
- A `new()`-built outcome renders the same hint as the built-in functions.

## 2. `DomainError::from_error`: keep a `thiserror` cause chain

### Problem

`impl std::error::Error for DomainError {}` (`crates/michi-core/src/error.rs`, around line 272) leaves `source()` as `None`, and there is no constructor from an existing error. A tool following the orin-dx convention of one `thiserror` enum per crate must walk `source()` by hand to avoid losing the cause chain when it builds a `DomainError`.

monokl's hand-written version is in `to_domain_error` (`/Users/gabe/Projects/monokl/.claude/worktrees/sibling-conventions/crates/monokl/src/output/agent.rs`, around lines 619-680). The message is the error's own `Display`. It walks `source()` and adds each link's `Display` as a hint, splitting every link on line breaks.

### Current state

- `DomainError` is `Clone`, and derives `schemars::JsonSchema` behind a feature.
- `render()` now quotes and escapes the message and hints (TOON 4.4), so splitting on line breaks is no longer needed for correct output.

### Proposed API

```rust
impl DomainError {
    /// `message` is `err`'s own Display; each `source()` link's Display becomes a hint, outermost first.
    pub fn from_error(code: ErrorCode, err: &(dyn std::error::Error + 'static)) -> Self;
}
```

### Decisions to make

- **Render-only, or also store the cause.**
  - Render-only is the API above and adds no field. The chain survives in the hints.
  - Storing the cause adds `source: Option<Arc<dyn Error + Send + Sync>>`, so `source()` works for Rust callers and `Clone` still works. It costs `#[schemars(skip)]`, a re-check of michi-core's `lib.rs` `Send + Sync` test, and an owned argument (`impl Error + Send + Sync + 'static`).
  - Recommendation: ship render-only, and add the stored cause when a consumer needs `source()`.
- **One hint per chain link, or one per line.** Now that michi escapes line breaks, one hint per link is simpler and loses nothing. Pick one and document it.
- **Message prefix.** monokl prefixes its own code (`walk: …`). Leave prefixing to the caller rather than adding a parameter.
- **Gate 3 evidence is thin.** Only monokl has hand-written this; callisto and caliper don't use michi and rely on miette's `#[diagnostic(transparent)]`. The case for building it now: it is a mechanical utility with no domain knowledge, and every `thiserror`-based consumer's first integration step needs it. If that does not clear the gate, record it and wait for a second consumer.

### Tests to write first

- A two-level `thiserror` chain gives the exact message and exactly one hint per cause, outermost first.
- An error with no source gives no hints.
- A multi-line cause renders as one escaped hint.
- With the `miette` feature, `help()` includes the chain.

## When these ship

Publish through Callisto as usual, and tell the monokl session the version. monokl will:

- Replace its `source()` walk in `to_domain_error` with `DomainError::from_error`, and drop `split_display_lines`.
- Use `TruncationOutcome` in its budget layer instead of rendering truncation markers in core.
- Delete `.claude/plans/MICHI-ADJUSTMENTS.md`.

# michi-core

## 0.4.0

- michi-core: public types can now grow in 0.4.x without breaking callers.
  
  - **Breaking:** `toon::Value`, `KvValue` and `RetryConfigError` are `#[non_exhaustive]`. A `match` on them outside michi-core needs a `_` arm.
  - **Breaking:** `FailedOp`, `PartialSuccess`, `KvItem`, `StatusItem`, `RecoveryHint`, `pipeline::PipelineStep` and `pipeline::Pipeline` are `#[non_exhaustive]`. Struct literals no longer compile outside michi-core; use the constructors below. Fields stay public, so reading and assigning them still works.
  - New constructors: `FailedOp::new(operation, reason)` with `.recovery(hint)`, `PartialSuccess::new(completed, failed, skipped)` and `PartialSuccess::default()`, `KvItem::new(key, value)`, `StatusItem::new(key, value)` with `.health(health)`, `PipelineStep::new(id, name, status)`, `Pipeline::new(id, steps)`. `RecoveryHint::new(tool)` is unchanged.
    - Before: `KvItem { key: "id".into(), value: KvValue::Int(1) }`
    - After: `KvItem::new("id", KvValue::Int(1))`
  - **Breaking (paths):** the crate root re-exports `resilience` and `truncate` items by explicit list instead of `pub use resilience::*` and `pub use truncate::*`. Every path that worked before still works (`michi_core::RetryConfig`, `michi_core::already_done`, `michi_core::truncate`, …); items added to those modules later appear only under their module.
  - `RetryConfig` and `toon::ToonOptions` implement `PartialEq`, `PipelineStep` and `Pipeline` implement `PartialEq` and `Eq`.
  - More functions are `#[must_use]` (for example `RecoveryHint::new`, `Hint::as_str`, `IdempotencyKey::as_str`), so discarding their result now warns.
- michi-core: values survive every wire, and invalid TOON is never emitted.
  
  - **Breaking (`schemars`):** `StatusResponse`, `StatusItem`, `Health`, `toon::ToonOptions`, `ErrorClass`, `KvItem`, `OutputFormat`, `pipeline::Pipeline` and `pipeline::PipelineStep` no longer implement `JsonSchema`. Nothing serializes them, so their schemas described no real wire form. Every remaining schema describes what serde emits.
  - `toon::Value::Float` NaN and ±Infinity now round-trip through serde as `"NaN"`, `"Infinity"` and `"-Infinity"` (they serialized as `null` and failed to read back), the same form `KvValue` uses. Rendered TOON still shows `null`, and the schema lists the three strings.
  - `Value::from(f32)` and f32 fields in `toon::list()` keep the f32's shortest digits: `0.1f32` renders `0.1`, not `0.10000000149011612`.
  - `AgentResponse` on the KV path with no items keeps a total count: `kv_items(vec![]).total_count(0)` renders `totalCount: 0` in the text and JSON body instead of an empty body.
  - `KvValue` NaN and ±Infinity round-trip through serde as named strings; the JSON companions write `null` for them, matching the TOON body, instead of the quoted strings `"NaN"`/`"inf"`.
  - `empty_state` with a reserved type name (`totalCount`, `help`, `recovery`) renders a `toon_validation_failed` error block instead of invalid TOON. New `try_empty_state` and `try_empty_state_with_hints` return the `ToonError`.
  - `RecoveryHint::param` replaces an existing key in place instead of adding a second one, and every renderer writes a repeated key once, so the JSON never holds duplicate keys.
  - MCP serde accepts what MCP allows: only `content` is required, `isError` defaults to `false`, `structuredContent` may be absent or `null`, and `annotations`/`audience` are optional. `structuredContent` is omitted when empty, and serializing a non-object `structuredContent` is an error instead of invalid MCP. New `CallToolResult::try_new` and `StructuredContentError`.
  - With `serde`, `DomainError` serializes to exactly the object `render_json()` writes, and its `schemars` schema describes that object.
  - GitHub annotations escape `%` (and `:`/`,` in the title), so a literal `%0A` in a message no longer becomes a line break.
  - `parse_retry_after` accepts the RFC 850 and asctime HTTP-date forms as well as IMF-fixdate.
  - `next_retry_delay` rounds `base_delay` and `retry_after` up to whole milliseconds, so a sub-millisecond delay no longer becomes zero.
  - Correction to the 0.3.0 notes: `toon::list()` rows missing a field get a `null` cell, not an empty one.
- Packaging and docs: the minimum supported Rust version is now 1.93 (was 1.96). The crates and npm packages ship their license text, michi-pipeline ships a README, docs.rs builds michi-core with the `serde`, `schemars` and `miette` features, the READMEs' links work on crates.io and npm, and michi-pipeline re-exports `RetryConfig`, `RetryConfigError`, `RetryBudget` and `IdempotencyKey`, so configuring retries needs no direct michi-core dependency.
- Report what a list cap cut, and keep an error's cause chain apart from its hints.
  
  - michi-core: new `TruncationOutcome<T>` (`kept`, `total_before`, `truncated()`, `omitted()`) reports what a cap on a list cut, however you chose the survivors. `truncate_by_count(items, max)` keeps the first `max`; `truncate_by_size(items, budget, size_of)` keeps items in order while your `size_of` (bytes, tokens, …) fits the budget. Wrap your own selection with `TruncationOutcome::new(kept, total_before)`. `hint(guidance)` returns `showing 2 of 5; {guidance}`, or `None` when nothing was cut.
  - michi-core: `AgentResponse::truncation(&outcome, guidance)` sets `totalCount` and adds that hint in one call, so the two always agree. Pass `outcome.kept` to `.items(...)` as before.
  - michi-core: `DomainError` has a `causes` field and a `.cause(text)` builder for why an error happened, separate from `hints` (what to do next). `render()` writes them as `causes[N]: …` after `message`; `render_json()`, serde and the JSON Schema add a `causes` array (`[]` when empty); with `miette`, `help()` lists them as `caused by: …` lines after the hints.
  - michi-core: `DomainError::from_error(code, &err)` takes the message from `err` and one cause per `source()` link, outermost first, skipping a link whose text the previous one already includes (common with `#[error("…: {0}")]`).
  - @orin-dx/michi: `renderDomainError` takes an optional fifth argument, `causes` (string array), rendered as `causes[N]: …`. Each cause is capped at 1 MiB and counts toward the call's 64 MiB limit.

## 0.3.1

- First published release. 0.3.0 was never published; its changes, listed below, ship in 0.3.1.
- Joined the `michi` group at this version.

## 0.3.0

- **Breaking:** `pipeline::StepStatus` gains `Running`, `CompletedEarlier`, `OutcomeUnknown(UnknownCause)`, `NotRun(NotRunReason)` and `Panicked`, and `Skipped` now carries a `SkipReason` (`PrerequisiteFailed` or `Cancelled`). The reason enums are `#[non_exhaustive]`. New `StepStatus::reason()` and `is_success()`; labels are snake_case (`completed_earlier`, `outcome_unknown`, `not_run`). With `serde`, the status types serialize in snake_case.
- **Breaking:** `Pipeline::render()` emits `step[N]{id,name,status,reason}:`, with the reason label or `null` in the new column. Output stays TOON 4.4 conformant.
- New `resilience::RetryBudget`: a pure retry budget modelled on tower's `TpsBudget` (each success deposits a fraction of a retry, each retry withdraws one, capped). `michi-pipeline` enforces it per run.

- `michi-core` now contains the whole synchronous library. The `michi-toon`, `michi-truncate` and `michi-resilience` crates and the `michi` facade are merged into it as the `toon`, `truncate` and `resilience` modules, and the NAPI exports move here behind the `napi` feature. Replace `michi::` paths with `michi_core::`; module paths are otherwise unchanged (`michi::toon::list` becomes `michi_core::toon::list`). `michi-core` and `michi-pipeline` now share one version.
- Quoted TOON cells double their backslashes (`C:\src\a,b` → `"C:\\src\\a,b"`). Before, backslashes were lost on parsing and a value ending in `\` merged two cells.
- Line breaks in caller text are written as `\n` / `\r` in every renderer instead of passing through raw (hints, empty-state names, error messages, recovery tool/reason/keys, KV keys, already-done fields, partial-success ids) or being dropped (KV values, status fields, TOON cells). TOON cells containing a line break are quoted. TOON hints keep ordinary punctuation instead of replacing `,` `[` `]` `{` `}` with `_`.
- `toon::list()` headers are the union of every item's fields in first-seen order; rows missing a field get an empty cell. Before, the first item decided the columns.
- `AgentResponse`: rows that fail TOON validation set `isError: true` in MCP results and the JSON render, not just in the text body. New `AgentResponse::is_error()`.
- `Value::from(u64)` / `Value::from(usize)` above `i64::MAX`, and such numbers in `toon::list()`, keep their exact digits (as the new numeric `Value::UInt`, never truncated or quoted) instead of clamping to `i64::MAX` or rounding through `f64`.
- `RecoveryHint` serializes as `{"tool", "params": {key: value}, "reason"?}`, matching the structured companions; `reason` is omitted when absent.
- The `schemars` schemas for `ContentBlock`, `CallToolResult` and `RecoveryHint` describe the wire form serde emits. The `schemars` feature now enables `serde`.
- Deserializing a `RecoveryHint` rejects parameter values it cannot hold exactly (arrays, objects, integers outside `i64`) instead of rewriting them; floats keep their exact value.
- Deserializing a `ContentBlock` whose `type` is not `"text"` is an error instead of a silent conversion to text.
- `Error::InvalidInput` / `Error::NotFound` renders escape line breaks like every other renderer.
- The default build no longer depends on serde: `compact_str`'s serde support is enabled only by the `serde` feature.
- Truncation reports what was cut: the suffix is `" ({removed} more chars — use {hint})"`, where `removed` is the number of chars cut, instead of `" ({original} chars truncated — use {hint})"`, which reported the original length although some chars remained. An empty hint now drops the `— use …` clause instead of printing `use )`.
- TOON cells no longer tell agents to use `full=true`, a parameter the calling tool may not have: a truncated cell ends with `" ({removed} more chars)"` unless the caller sets the new `ToonOptions::truncation_hint` / `AgentResponse::truncation_hint` (NAPI: `JsToonOptions.truncationHint`, `AgentResponse.truncationHint()`). Pass `.truncation_hint("full=true")` to keep the old clause.
- A cap too small for the suffix gives the first `max_chars - 1` chars and `…` (`signal` is `"…"`) instead of a fragment such as `" (500 chars tr"`; a cap of 0 still gives the empty string.
- Documented that `max_cell_len` / `truncate_cells_at` count chars before TOON escaping and quoting, so a quoted cell can be longer, and that `Truncated::original_len` is a byte length.
- Every agent-facing block is now a TOON 4.4 document, not only lists, and no block ends with a newline. `render_hints`, `append_hints`, `render_kv`, `render_recovery`, `append_recovery`, `DomainError::render`, `Error::render`, `StatusResponse::render`, `PartialSuccess::render` and `render_already_done` return a finished document; `append_hints`/`append_recovery` add one LF before the block unless the buffer is empty or already ends in one. Code that concatenated blocks relying on the trailing newline must join them with `\n` or use the append helpers.
  - KV: one space after each colon instead of column alignment; keys and text values quoted per TOON §7.3/§7.2 (`note: "a: b"`); `Missing` is `null` instead of `—`; `Float(f, decimals)` rounds to `decimals` places and then drops trailing zeros (`Float(1.5, 3)` → `1.5`, not `1.500`; NaN/±Infinity → `null`). `Duration` stays `1.5s`.
  - **Breaking:** `render_kv` returns `Result<String, KvError>`. New `KvError` (`ReservedKey`, `DuplicateKey`) rejects a repeated key and the keys `totalCount`, `help` and `recovery`, which would duplicate a root key. `AgentResponse`'s KV path renders such items as an `error: kv_validation_failed` body and sets `is_error`; NAPI `renderKv` throws `kv_validation_failed: …`.
  - **Breaking:** a TOON type name `recovery` is rejected (`ToonError::InvalidTypeName`) like `totalCount` and `help`, since `AgentResponse` appends a `recovery` table.
  - Recovery hints: `recovery[N]:` with `  tool: suggestedParams: { k: v } — reason` lines → the table `recovery[N]{tool,params,reason}:` with `params` as the quoted compact JSON object (`"{\"user\":\"alice\"}"`, `"{}"` when empty) and `reason` `null` when absent.
  - Status: `tool:        x` / `key:   value  [DEGRADED: reason]` → `tool: x`, `description: …` and the table `items[N]{key,value,health,reason}:` (`items: []` when empty). `health` is `ok`, `degraded`, `error`, or `null` when the item has no health signal, so `Health::Ok` and `None` no longer render identically.
  - Errors: `message` is quoted when §7.2 requires it. `Error::InvalidInput(m)` / `Error::NotFound(m)` render `error: invalid_input` / `error: not_found`, `message: m`, `exit_code: 1` — the `DomainError` shape — instead of `error: Invalid input: m`.
  - Partial success: the summary is quoted (`partial_success: "2 completed, 1 failed, 1 skipped"`), `completed`/`skipped` are inline arrays (`completed[2]: a,b`), and the failed operations' recovery hints are a `recovery[N]{tool,params,reason}:` table instead of a `help[N]:` block.
  - `render_already_done`: `status:    already_done` → `status: already_done`; `operation`/`summary` quoted per §7.2.
- serde_json's `float_roundtrip` feature is enabled with the `serde` feature, so deserialized floats are correctly rounded.

## 0.1.1

- Dependency updates
  - `michi-toon` → `0.2.0`

## Merged history: michi-toon 0.2.0

- `render_toon()` now returns `Result<String, ToonError>` instead of `String`. monokl is on michi-core 0.4.0. Its error conversion now uses michi's `DomainError::from_error` instead of a hand-written loop, and `just ci` passes (271 tests, 98.6% line coverage). It's pushed to PR https://github.com/orin-dx/monokl/pull/3 as commit 79bf9e6.

- **No breaking changes reached monokl:** the newly `#[non_exhaustive]` types (`toon::Value`, `RecoveryHint` and others) didn't affect its code, and clippy is clean.
- **Errors carry causes now.** An error's chain of underlying errors goes into michi's new `causes` field rather than being added as hints. Hints are now only monokl's own advice, such as "you supplied 12 terms; the limit is 8".
- **Multi-line messages stay whole.** michi escapes the line breaks, so a multi-line error still renders as three lines. monokl's line-splitting helper is gone.
- **Changed agent output:** a git error spanning several lines used to arrive as a first-line message plus extra hints. It's now a single escaped message. A wrapped error's text now appears as `causes[N]: …` rather than in `help[N]: …`.
- **Tests:** I rewrote three tests for the new model. One new test checks that an `Io` error reports its underlying I/O error as a cause exactly once, which relies on `from_error` skipping repeated text.
- **`TruncationOutcome` isn't used yet.** monokl has no budget layer to plug it into. It's ready for when the budget work starts, and replaces the truncation-marker strings the spec bans from core.

`MICHI-ADJUSTMENTS.md` in your main checkout is now fully resolved and can be deleted. B and C1 shipped, A1–A5 were fixed in 0.3.1, and D1 was never requested.

content.content:
## 0.6.0

- Breaking: michi-core now uses `compact_str` 0.10 (was 0.8). `toon::Value::Str` holds a 0.10 `CompactString` and `From<CompactString> for Value` takes one, so code that builds these from its own `CompactString` must upgrade `compact_str` to 0.10. Conversions from `&str` and `String` are unchanged.
- Breaking for users of the `schemars` feature: michi-core now implements schemars 1.x's `JsonSchema` (was 0.8). Upgrade your own `schemars` dependency to 1.x; `schemars::gen::SchemaGenerator` and `schemars::schema::Schema` are now `schemars::SchemaGenerator` and `schemars::Schema`.
  
  Generated schemas are JSON Schema 2020-12 instead of draft-07. They describe the same wire form, spelled differently: subschemas under `$defs`, `const` for unit variants, `prefixItems` for tuples, and a `$ref` beside `default` without an `allOf` wrapper.

## 0.5.0

- Fix review findings: a per-object byte budget for Node's `AgentResponse`, tiny floats that rendered `0`, schemas that disagreed with serde, and retry defaults that claimed a timeout was safe to retry.
  
  - @orin-dx/michi: one `AgentResponse` now holds at most 64 MiB of strings across all its calls, not 64 MiB per call (65 separate 1 MiB hints were accepted and rendered 68 MB). Replacing `items`, `kvItems`, `truncationHint` or `humanContent` gives the old value's bytes back. Over the total, a call throws `cumulative byte total N exceeds maximum of 67108864` and leaves the builder unchanged. The constructor's `typeName` and `emptyState`'s `typeName` are capped at 4 KiB, `humanContent` at 1 MiB.
  - michi-core, @orin-dx/michi: floats needing more than 255 decimal places no longer render `0`. Without `decimalsVal`, `1e-300` and `5e-324` render as themselves. New `KvValue::FULL_PRECISION` (255) never rounds, in TOON and the JSON companions; a smaller decimals count still rounds as asked.
  - michi-core: `RecoveryHint` deserialization accepts floats of any size (tiny ones such as `1e-300` were rejected) and integers past `i64::MAX` that have an exact float form, so a hint's own serialized floats (`Float(1e19, 0)`) read back. An integer past `i64::MAX` that would be rounded (`18446744073709551615`) is still rejected; send it as a string. The schema says so in its description.
  - michi-core: the JSON Schemas of `KvValue::Int`, `toon::Value::Int`, `toon::Value::UInt` and `KvValue::Float`'s decimals state the bounds serde enforces.
  - michi-core: `DomainError::new` defaults `retryable` to `false` for `Timeout` and `ExternalFailure` (it was `true`): the request may have taken effect. `retryable` means calling again is expected to help without repeating an effect; pass `.retryable(true)` when the operation is idempotent. `RateLimited` and `Unavailable` stay retryable. A `Timeout` not marked retryable is the new `ErrorClass::Ambiguous` (it was classed `Transient` through the old default), and carries the hint `MAY_HAVE_TAKEN_EFFECT_HINT` until `.retryable(true)` removes it. `is_retryable_status` documents that 502 and 504 are safe to retry only for idempotent requests.
  - michi-core, @orin-dx/michi: `parse_retry_after` treats a pre-1970 HTTP-date as a past date (zero delay), rejects unpadded or signed digit fields such as `+8:+9:+7`, and saturates delay-seconds past `u64::MAX` instead of returning `None`.
  - michi-core: rendering recovery params with repeated-key de-duplication is linear (40,000 params took 1.77 s).
  - michi-core: `MAX_CELLS` counts one cell per row when a list has no fields, so `toon::list` of millions of empty items is rejected with `TooManyCells`.
- michi-pipeline: retries and resume no longer repeat an effect that may already have landed.
  
  - **Breaking:** `ExecutionError::Failed` has a third field, `effect: Effect` (`NotApplied` or `Unknown`). Build it with the new constructors: `failed(msg)` (not retryable, effect unknown, the default), `refused(msg)` (not retryable, not applied), `rejected(msg)` (retryable, not applied) or `transient(msg)` (retryable, effect unknown). `ExecutionError::effect()` reports the effect of any error.
  - **Breaking:** a non-idempotent step that fails with an unknown effect (`failed(msg)`, an HTTP 500 or other 5xx) now ends `OutcomeUnknown(StepFailed)`, not `Failed`, and resume holds it until verified. Before, resume ran it again and could commit twice. Use `refused(msg)` for failures that certainly had no effect.
  - **Breaking:** `ReplayClass::Definitive` is replaced by `Refused` (not applied) and `Ambiguous` (effect unknown).
  - **Breaking:** `ExecutionError::refused` counts as healthy for the circuit breaker (like an HTTP 4xx), so validation failures no longer open it. `PlanFingerprint` parses only 16 lowercase hex digits (it used to accept a leading `+` and uppercase).
  - Precheck: a `Replay::Prechecked` step implements `Step::precheck`, which runs before every attempt and answers `Precheck::Applied` (the step ends `CompletedEarlier` without running), `NotApplied` (it runs) or `Unknown` (it doesn't; `NotRun(Unverified)` if nothing ran yet). Resume uses it instead of a manual verdict.
  - Durable starts: `ExecOptions::durable_starts(observer)` takes a `DurableObserver`, and a step runs only after its `record_start` saves the in-flight marker; if that fails or panics, the step ends `NotRun(StartNotRecorded)` without being invoked. This closes the gap where a crash rebuilt a step that ran as `Pending`.
  - Records saved by 0.4 still load: a `Failed` error without `effect` reads as `Unknown`, and the attempt class `definitive` reads as `Ambiguous`, so resume holds such steps instead of re-running them.
  
  michi-core: `UnknownCause::StepFailed` (rendered `step_failed`) and `NotRunReason::{Unverified, StartNotRecorded}` (rendered `unverified`, `start_not_recorded`), on enums that were already `#[non_exhaustive]`. `@orin-dx/michi`'s `renderPipeline` accepts the three new reasons.

  - **Breaking:** `ReplayClass::Definitive` is replaced by `Refused` (not applied) and `Ambiguous` (effect unknown).
  - **Breaking:** `ExecutionError::refused` counts as healthy for the circuit breaker (like an HTTP 4xx), so validation failures no longer open it. `PlanFingerprint` parses only 16 lowercase hex digits (it used to accept a leading `+` and uppercase).
  - Precheck: a `Replay::Prechecked` step implements `Step::precheck`, which runs before every attempt and answers `Precheck::Applied` (the step ends `CompletedEarlier` without running), `NotApplied` (it runs) or `Unknown` (it doesn't; `NotRun(Unverified)` if nothing ran yet). Resume uses it instead of a manual verdict.
  - Durable starts: `ExecOptions::durable_starts(observer)` takes a `DurableObserver`, and a step runs only after its `record_start` saves the in-flight marker; if that fails or panics, the step ends `NotRun(StartNotRecorded)` without being invoked. This closes the gap where a crash rebuilt a step that ran as `Pending`.
  - Records saved by 0.4 still load: a `Failed` error without `effect` reads as `Unknown`, and the attempt class `definitive` reads as `Ambiguous`, so resume holds such steps instead of re-running them.
  
  michi-core: `UnknownCause::StepFailed` (rendered `step_failed`) and `NotRunReason::{Unverified, StartNotRecorded}` (rendered `unverified`, `start_not_recorded`), on enums that were already `#[non_exhaustive]`. `@orin-dx/michi`'s `renderPipeline` accepts the three new reasons.

# callisto configuration

[changesets]
dir = ".changeset"

[cascade]
mode = "out-of-range"
bump-severity = "patch"
peer-escalation = true
preserve-npm-ranges = true

# Rust library crates, published to crates.io.
[[package]]
match = "cargo/michi-core"
# One GitHub release per version for the whole group, attached here and tagged michi@{version}. Callisto keeps a tag
# per package (it finds each package's last release from its own tag and rejects a shared tag, E194), so the other
# members keep {name}@{version}; this mirrors Callisto's own callisto@{version} release tag.
publish-to = ["crates-io", "github-release"]
release-trigger = "changeset"
tag-template = "michi@{version}"
previous-tag-templates = ["michi-core@{version}"]

[[package]]
match = "cargo/michi-pipeline"
publish-to = ["crates-io"]
release-trigger = "changeset"

# MIT graph crate, released with the rest of michi (one version for every michi package).
[[package]]
match = "cargo/michi-graph"
publish-to = ["crates-io"]
release-trigger = "changeset"

# michi-node: NAPI cdylib + npm package
[[package]]
match = "npm/michi-node"
publish-to = ["npm"]
release-trigger = "changeset"

# Every michi package ships one version: a change to any of them releases all four.
[[fixed-group]]
name = "michi"
members = ["cargo/michi-core", "cargo/michi-graph", "cargo/michi-pipeline", "npm/@orin-dx/michi"]

content.content:
name: Release

# Callisto's build-matrix release flow for napi platform packages
# (docs/releasing.md in orin-dx/callisto): a push to main either refreshes the
# Callisto version PR or, for a merged version PR, runs plan -> build ->
# execute. Keep this filename: Callisto's recovery docs and coordinator
# identity name `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      release_source_sha:
        description: 'Merged Callisto version-PR commit to recover; leave empty for the triggering commit.'
        required: false
        type: string

permissions: {}

# One group per commit: GitHub replaces a pending run in a shared group, which
# could silently drop a release merge queued behind an unrelated push.
concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  release-candidate:
    name: Identify a merged Callisto version PR
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      is_release: ${{ steps.decision.outputs.is_release }}
      release_source_sha: ${{ steps.provenance.outputs.release_source_sha }}
      orchestration_sha: ${{ steps.provenance.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
    steps:
      # Scheduling only: `callisto release plan` verifies the actual
      # parent-to-merge delta. A release must also be a GitHub-verified merge
      # of the managed PR, never a direct push.
      - name: Check release-source provenance
        id: provenance
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA_INPUT: ${{ inputs.release_source_sha }}
          TRIGGERING_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          release_source_sha="${RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA_INPUT:-$TRIGGERING_SHA}"
          if [[ ! "$release_source_sha" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::release_source_sha must be exactly 40 lowercase hex characters"
            exit 1
          fi
          resolved_sha=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}" --jq '.sha')
          if [[ "$resolved_sha" != "$release_source_sha" ]]; then
            echo "::error::release_source_sha does not resolve to that exact commit"
            exit 1
          fi
          # gh rejects --slurp together with --jq, so slurp the pages and filter with jq.
          prs=$(gh api --paginate --slurp "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}/pulls" |
            jq --arg repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" '[.[][] | select(.merged_at != null and .base.ref == "main" and
              .head.repo.full_name == $repo and
              (.head.ref == "callisto/version-packages" or
               (.head.ref | test("^callisto/version-packages--[0-9a-f]{40}$"))))] | length')
          verified=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${release_source_sha}" \
            --jq '.commit.verification.verified')
          managed=false
          if [[ "$prs" == 1 && "$verified" == true ]]; then managed=true; fi
          {
            echo "managed=$managed"
            echo "release_source_sha=$release_source_sha"
            # The current run coordinates; a recovery never reruns historic workflow code.
            echo "orchestration_sha=$TRIGGERING_SHA"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: steps.provenance.outputs.managed == 'true'
        with:
          ref: ${{ steps.provenance.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 2
          persist-credentials: false

      # `release plan --from-release-commit` requires the commit to write its
      # release decision. A managed PR without one (e.g. a workflow fix merged
      # from a callisto/ branch) refreshes the version PR instead.
      - name: Check for a release decision
        id: decision
        env:
          MANAGED: ${{ steps.provenance.outputs.managed }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          is_release=false
          if [[ "$MANAGED" == true ]] && git rev-parse --verify --quiet HEAD^ > /dev/null &&
            git diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-only --diff-filter=AM -r HEAD^ HEAD | grep -qxF .callisto/release-decision.json; then
            is_release=true
          fi
          echo "is_release=$is_release" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  version-pr:
    name: Create or update the Callisto version PR
    needs: release-candidate
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release != 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    concurrency:
      group: callisto-version-pr
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      # The default version command (`callisto version`) refreshes lockfiles
      # and the action appends --emit-decision .callisto/release-decision.json.
      - uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-action@c3d524d3aba359f5e767007ea76d229e8a291dc3 # callisto@0.12.0
        with:
          mode: version-pr
          version: callisto@0.12.0
          branch: main
          release_branch: callisto/version-packages
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

  plan:
    name: Plan the release from the merged version PR
    needs: release-candidate
    if: needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.matrix }}
      napi_dir: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.napi_dir }}
      has_napi: ${{ steps.matrix.outputs.has_napi }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/setup-callisto@c3d524d3aba359f5e767007ea76d229e8a291dc3 # callisto@0.12.0
        with:
          version: callisto@0.12.0

      - name: Plan the release
        env:
          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          ORCHESTRATION_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent"
          callisto release plan --from-release-commit "$RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA" --decision .callisto/release-decision.json \
            --orchestration-revision "$ORCHESTRATION_SHA" --artifact-repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
            --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json"
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent" && shasum -a 256 release-intent.json > release-intent.json.sha256)

      - name: Build the matrix from the intent's napi targets
        id: matrix
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          intent="$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json"
          # This workflow builds napi addons only. Artifact slots or PyPI
          # publishes need the generated workflow's artifact-manifest path.
          if ! jq -e '(.artifactSlots // []) == [] and
            ([.operations[].id.package | select(startswith("pypi/"))] == [])' "$intent" > /dev/null; then
            echo "::error::the release intent declares artifact slots or PyPI publishes, which this workflow does not build"
            exit 1
          fi
          # Only packages in the release intent: an unrelated addon adds no build.
          {
            while IFS= read -r package; do
              callisto --format json matrix --package "$package"
            done < <(jq -r '[.operations[].id.package] | unique[]' "$intent")
          } | jq -s '{platformTargets: (map(.platformTargets) | add // {})}' > "$RUNNER_TEMP/matrix.json"
          # Callisto 0.11 schedules x86_64-apple-darwin on macos-13, a retired
          # runner image: build it on the arm64 macos-latest instead, where
          # rustup's x86_64-apple-darwin target links with Apple's universal SDK.
          # Every other target keeps Callisto's hostRunner/useCross (aarch64
          # Linux cross-compiles with cargo-zigbuild on ubuntu-latest).
          matrix=$(jq -c '[.platformTargets[] | select(.kind == "napi") | .targets[]] | unique_by(.artifactName) |
            map(if .triple == "x86_64-apple-darwin" then .hostRunner = "macos-latest" | .useCross = false else . end)' \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/matrix.json")
          # Execute places one package's JS binding; a second addon needs per-package placement. A release with no
          # addon (michi-graph on its own, say) skips the build and placement entirely.
          napi_dirs=$(jq -c '[.[].packageDir] | unique' <<< "$matrix")
          case $(jq length <<< "$napi_dirs") in
            0) has_napi=false napi_dir="" ;;
            1) has_napi=true napi_dir=$(jq -r '.[0]' <<< "$napi_dirs") ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::expected at most one napi package directory, got $napi_dirs"
              exit 1
              ;;
          esac
          {
            echo "matrix=$matrix"
            echo "napi_dir=$napi_dir"
            echo "has_napi=$has_napi"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

  build:
    name: Build ${{ matrix.triple }}
    needs: [release-candidate, plan]
    # An empty matrix is an error in GitHub Actions, so a release without an addon skips the job instead.
    if: needs.plan.outputs.has_napi == 'true'
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include: ${{ fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.matrix) }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.hostRunner }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
    env:
      TRIPLE: ${{ matrix.triple }}
      USE_CROSS: ${{ matrix.useCross }}
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: ${{ matrix.packageDir }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Install the Rust target
        run: rustup target add "$TRIPLE"

      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-proto-node-pnpm@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          working-directory: ${{ matrix.packageDir }}
          cache: 'false'

      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      # napi's --cross-compile links non-native Linux targets with cargo-zigbuild.
      - name: Install zig
        if: matrix.useCross
        run: pip install ziglang

      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@8cca0918f8471c33515202b73f56ab27f2bed283 # v2
        if: matrix.useCross
        with:
          tool: cargo-zigbuild

      # --output-dir keeps the checkout clean; napi writes the .node file and
      # the generated index.js/index.d.ts there.
      - name: Build the napi addon
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          args=(--release --target "$TRIPLE" --output-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/napi-out")
          if [[ "$USE_CROSS" == true ]]; then args+=(--cross-compile); fi
          pnpm build "${args[@]}"

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: napi-${{ matrix.artifactName }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/napi-out/*.node
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

      # index.js and index.d.ts are gitignored build outputs the npm package ships.
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: binding-${{ matrix.artifactName }}
          path: |
            ${{ runner.temp }}/napi-out/index.js
            ${{ runner.temp }}/napi-out/index.d.ts
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

  execute:
    name: Execute the planned release
    needs: [release-candidate, plan, build]
    # !cancelled() rather than always(): cancelling the run must stop the one irreversible job.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.plan.result == 'success' &&
      (needs.build.result == 'success' || (needs.build.result == 'skipped' && needs.plan.outputs.has_napi == 'false'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    concurrency:
      group: callisto-release-execute
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          # Callisto pushes the release tags from this checkout.
          persist-credentials: true # zizmor: ignore[artipacked]

      - uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/setup-callisto@c3d524d3aba359f5e767007ea76d229e8a291dc3 # callisto@0.12.0
        with:
          version: callisto@0.12.0

      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-proto-node-pnpm@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        if: needs.plan.outputs.has_napi == 'true'
        with:
          working-directory: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.napi_dir }}
          cache: 'false'

      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
        if: needs.plan.outputs.has_napi == 'true'
        working-directory: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.napi_dir }}

      # Downloads land under $RUNNER_TEMP: `release execute` requires a clean worktree.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        if: needs.plan.outputs.has_napi == 'true'
        with:
          pattern: napi-*
          merge-multiple: true
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/napi-artifacts

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        if: needs.plan.outputs.has_napi == 'true'
        with:
          pattern: binding-*
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/napi-bindings

      # Everything placed here is gitignored, so the checkout stays clean:
      # the .node files go into the committed npm/<platform> package dirs.
      - name: Verify the handoff
        run: (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent" && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)

      - name: Place the napi artifacts
        if: needs.plan.outputs.has_napi == 'true'
        working-directory: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.napi_dir }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          bindings=("$RUNNER_TEMP"/napi-bindings/*)
          for binding in "${bindings[@]}"; do
            cmp "${bindings[0]}/index.js" "$binding/index.js"
            cmp "${bindings[0]}/index.d.ts" "$binding/index.d.ts"
          done
          cp "${bindings[0]}/index.js" "${bindings[0]}/index.d.ts" .
          # napi 3.7 joins --output-dir onto the package directory, so pass it relative.
          pnpm exec napi artifacts --output-dir "$(realpath --relative-to="$PWD" "$RUNNER_TEMP/napi-artifacts")"
          for manifest in npm/*/package.json; do
            binary="$(dirname "$manifest")/$(jq -r .main "$manifest")"
            if [[ ! -f "$binary" ]]; then
              echo "::error::missing napi artifact $binary"
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          if [[ -n "$(git status --porcelain)" ]]; then
            git status --porcelain
            echo "::error::artifact placement dirtied the release checkout"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Execute the release
        env:
          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
          NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: 'true'
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          ORCHESTRATION_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Callisto hands this config only to its npm publishers; the token
          # stays an ${NPM_TOKEN} reference, never written to disk.
          # shellcheck disable=SC2016
          printf '//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NPM_TOKEN}\n' > "$RUNNER_TEMP/callisto-npmrc"
          chmod 600 "$RUNNER_TEMP/callisto-npmrc"
          export CALLISTO_PUBLISH_NPM_CONFIG="$RUNNER_TEMP/callisto-npmrc"
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt"
          callisto release execute --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" \
            --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt/release-receipt.json" \
            --orchestration-revision "$ORCHESTRATION_SHA"

      - name: Summarize the receipt
        if: always()
        run: |
          receipt="$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt/release-receipt.json"
          if [[ -f "$receipt" ]]; then
            {
              echo '### Release receipt'
              echo '```json'
              cat "$receipt"
              echo '```'
            } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: always()
        with:
          # Per attempt: a re-run keeps each attempt's receipt instead of shadowing it.
          name: release-receipt-attempt-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-receipt
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 30
